sentences.zh: 劉臺，字子畏，安福人。

translations.literal: Liu Tai, styled Ziwei, was a man of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tai, styled Ziwei, was a native of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Longqing.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，改御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli, he was changed to censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Wanli reign, he was transferred to the post of censor.

sentences.zh: 巡按遼東，坐誤奏捷，奉旨譙責。

translations.literal: While inspecting Liaodong, he was punished for erroneously memorializing a victory and received an imperial reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as touring inspector of Liaodong, he was faulted for incorrectly reporting a military victory and received an imperial reprimand.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，臺上疏劾輔臣張居正，曰：

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Tai submitted a memorial impeaching the assisting minister Zhang Juzheng, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, Tai submitted a memorial impeaching Chief Minister Zhang Juzheng, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣聞進言者皆望陛下以堯、舜，而不聞責輔臣以臯、夔。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that those who offer counsel all hope Your Majesty will be like Yao and Shun, but has not heard anyone demand that the assisting minister be like Gao and Qi.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that those who offer counsel all hope Your Majesty will be like Yao and Shun, but I have not heard anyone demand that the chief minister be like Gao Yao and Qi.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 陛下有納諫之明，而輔臣無容言之量也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has the discernment to accept remonstrance, but the assisting minister lacks the magnanimity to allow speech.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has the discernment to accept remonstrance, but the chief minister lacks the magnanimity to tolerate open speech.

sentences.zh: 高皇帝鑒前代之失，不設丞相，事歸部院，勢不相攝，而職易稱。

translations.literal: The August Emperor, reflecting on the failures of previous ages, did not establish a chancellor; affairs returned to ministries and boards, their powers did not check one another, and offices were easy to fulfill.
translations.idiomatic: The August Emperor, taking warning from the failures of earlier dynasties, abolished the chancellorship and entrusted affairs to the ministries and boards, whose powers did not restrain one another and whose duties were easier to discharge.

sentences.zh: 文皇帝始置內閣，參預機務。

translations.literal: The Literary Emperor first established the Grand Secretariat to participate in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Literary Emperor first established the Grand Secretariat to take part in confidential state business.

sentences.zh: 其時官階未峻，無專肆之萌。

translations.literal: At that time official rank was not yet exalted, and there was no sprouting of arbitrary power.
translations.idiomatic: At that time official rank was not yet exalted, and there was no seed of arbitrary power.

sentences.zh: 二百年來，即有擅作威福者，尚惴惴然避宰相之名而不敢居，以祖宗之法在也。

translations.literal: Over two hundred years, even when there were those who monopolized authority and favor, they still trembled and avoided the name of prime minister and dared not claim it, because the laws of the ancestors remained.
translations.idiomatic: For two hundred years afterward, even those who monopolized authority and favor still trembled at the name of prime minister and dared not claim it, because the laws of the ancestors still stood.

sentences.zh: 乃大學士張居正偃然以相自處，自高拱被逐，擅威福者三四年矣。

translations.literal: Yet Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng presumes to conduct himself as prime minister; since Gao Gong was driven out, he has monopolized authority and favor for three or four years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng presumes to act as prime minister; since Gao Gong was driven from office, he has monopolized authority and favor for three or four years.

sentences.zh: 諫官因事論及，必曰：「吾守祖宗法。」

translations.literal: When remonstrating officials raise matters in discussion, he always says, "I keep the laws of the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: When remonstrating officials raise any matter, he always says, "I am keeping the laws of the ancestors."

sentences.zh: 臣請即以祖宗法正之。

translations.literal: Your servant begs to hold him to account by those very laws.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to hold him to account by those very laws.

sentences.zh: 祖宗進退大臣以禮。

translations.literal: The ancestors advanced and dismissed great ministers with propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestors advanced and dismissed great ministers with due propriety.

sentences.zh: 先帝臨崩，居正托疾以逐拱，既又文致之王大臣獄。

translations.literal: When the late emperor was on his deathbed, Juzheng feigned illness to drive out Gong, and afterward fabricated charges to place Wang Dachen in prison.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor lay dying, Juzheng feigned illness to drive out Gao Gong, and afterward fabricated charges to place Wang Dachen in prison.

sentences.zh: 及正論籍籍，則抵拱書，令勿驚死。

translations.literal: When upright opinion was widespread, he sent a letter to Gong telling him not to die of fright.
translations.idiomatic: When upright opinion grew widespread, he sent Gao Gong a letter telling him not to die of fright.

sentences.zh: 既迫逐以示威，又遺書以市德，徒使朝廷無禮於舊臣。

translations.literal: Having driven him out to show power, he also sent a letter to purchase virtue, merely leaving the court without propriety toward an old minister.
translations.idiomatic: Having driven him out to display his power, he also sent a letter to purchase goodwill, leaving the court without propriety toward a former minister.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之法若是乎？

translations.literal: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?

sentences.zh: 祖宗朝，非開國元勛，生不公，死不王。

translations.literal: In the age of the ancestors, unless one were a founding merit-holder, in life one was not enfeoffed as duke, in death one was not given the title of king.
translations.idiomatic: Under the ancestors, unless one were a founding merit-holder, no one was enfeoffed as duke in life or given the title of king after death.

sentences.zh: 成國公朱希忠，生非有奇功也，居正違祖訓，贈以王爵。

translations.literal: Duke of Chengguo Zhu Xizhong had no extraordinary merit in life, yet Juzheng violated ancestral instruction and ennobled him with the title of king.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Chengguo Zhu Xizhong had performed no extraordinary service in life, yet Juzheng violated ancestral instruction and posthumously granted him the title of king.

sentences.zh: 給事中陳吾德一言而外遷，郎中陳有年一爭而斥去。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Chen Wude spoke one word and was transferred away; Bureau Director Chen Younian disputed once and was expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Chen Wude spoke up once and was transferred away; Bureau Director Chen Younian objected once and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 臣恐公侯之家，布賄厚施，緣例陳乞，將無底極。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that in the houses of dukes and marquises, spreading bribes and lavish gifts, citing precedent to petition, there will be no limit.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that in the houses of dukes and marquises, lavish bribery and gifts, with petitions citing precedent, will know no limit.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之法若是乎？

translations.literal: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?

sentences.zh: 祖宗朝，用內閣冢宰，必由廷推。

translations.literal: In the age of the ancestors, appointing a Grand Secretariat chief minister had to be by court recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Under the ancestors, appointing a chief minister of the Grand Secretariat required recommendation by the court.

sentences.zh: 今居正私薦用張四維、張瀚。

translations.literal: Now Juzheng privately recommended and appointed Zhang Siwei and Zhang Han.
translations.idiomatic: Now Juzheng has privately recommended and appointed Zhang Siwei and Zhang Han.

sentences.zh: 四維在翰林，被論者數矣。

translations.literal: Siwei was in the Hanlin Academy and had been criticized several times.
translations.idiomatic: Siwei had served in the Hanlin Academy and had been criticized on several occasions.

sentences.zh: 其始去也，不任教習庶吉士也。

translations.literal: When he first left, he was not allowed to instruct the Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: When he first left office, he was not even allowed to instruct the Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 四維之為人也，居正知之熟矣。

translations.literal: As for what sort of man Siwei is, Juzheng knows it thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng knows full well what sort of man Siwei is.

sentences.zh: 知之而顧用之，夫亦以四維善機權，多憑藉，自念親老，旦暮不測，二三年間謀起復，任四維，其身後托乎？

translations.literal: Knowing this yet still employing him—was it not because Siwei is skilled in maneuver and has many connections, and Juzheng, thinking his parents are old and the morrow uncertain, plans within two or three years to seek restoration and entrust Siwei with his affairs after death?
translations.idiomatic: Knowing this yet still employing him—surely it is because Siwei is skilled at maneuvering and has many connections, and Juzheng, mindful that his parents are old and tomorrow uncertain, plans within two or three years to seek restoration and entrust his affairs after death to Siwei?

sentences.zh: 瀚生平無善狀。

translations.literal: Han had no good record in life.
translations.idiomatic: Han had no record of merit throughout his life.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陜西，贓穢狼籍。

translations.literal: As grand coordinator of Shaanxi, his corruption was notorious.
translations.idiomatic: As grand coordinator of Shaanxi, his corruption was notorious.

sentences.zh: 及驟躇銓衡，唯諾若簿吏，官缺必請命居正。

translations.literal: When he suddenly occupied the post of Minister of Personnel, he assented like a clerk; for every vacancy he had to request Juzheng's command.
translations.idiomatic: When he suddenly took charge of the Ministry of Personnel, he assented like a clerk; for every vacancy he had to seek Juzheng's orders.

sentences.zh: 所指授者，非楚人親戚知識，則親戚所援引也；

translations.literal: Those he appointed were either Chu natives who were relatives or acquaintances, or those whom relatives had recommended;
translations.idiomatic: Those he appointed were either natives of Chu who were relatives or acquaintances, or men whom relatives had recommended;

sentences.zh: 非宦楚受恩私故，則恩故之黨助也。

translations.literal: or else those who had served in Chu and received private favors, or the faction of such benefactors.
translations.idiomatic: or else men who had served in Chu and received private favors, or the factions of such benefactors.

sentences.zh: 瀚惟日取四方小吏，權其賄賂，而其他則徒擁虛名。

translations.literal: Han only daily took petty officials from the four directions and weighed their bribes, while in other matters he merely held an empty title.
translations.idiomatic: Han spent his days extracting bribes from petty officials sent from every quarter, while in all other matters he merely held an empty title.

sentences.zh: 聞居正貽南京都御史趙錦書，臺諫毋議及冢宰，則居正之脅制在朝言官，又可知矣。

translations.literal: It is heard that Juzheng sent a letter to Nanjing Censor-in-Chief Zhao Jin telling censors and remonstrators not to discuss the chief minister—thus Juzheng's coercion of remonstrating officials at court is again plain.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Juzheng sent Nanjing Censor-in-Chief Zhao Jin a letter telling censors and remonstrators not to discuss the chief minister—so his coercion of remonstrating officials at court is plain enough.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之法如是乎？

translations.literal: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?

sentences.zh: 祖宗朝，詔令不便，部臣猶訾閣擬之不審。

translations.literal: In the age of the ancestors, when an edict was inconvenient, ministry officials still criticized the Secretariat draft as not carefully considered.
translations.idiomatic: Under the ancestors, when an edict was ill-advised, ministry officials still criticized the Grand Secretariat draft as insufficiently considered.

sentences.zh: 今得一嚴旨，居正輒曰「我力調劑故止是」；

translations.literal: Now when a severe edict is obtained, Juzheng always says, "Through my exertions in adjusting matters it stopped at this";
translations.idiomatic: Now whenever a severe edict is issued, Juzheng always says, "Through my exertions in adjusting matters it stopped at this";

sentences.zh: 得一溫旨，居正又曰「我力請而後得之」。

translations.literal: when a mild edict is obtained, Juzheng again says, "I strenuously requested it and only then obtained it."
translations.idiomatic: whenever a mild edict is issued, he again says, "I strenuously requested it and only then obtained it."

sentences.zh: 由是畏居正者甚於畏陛下，感居正者甚於感陛下。

translations.literal: Hence those who fear Juzheng fear him more than they fear Your Majesty, and those who feel gratitude toward Juzheng feel it more than toward Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Hence officials fear Juzheng more than they fear Your Majesty, and feel gratitude toward him more than toward Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 威福自己，目無朝廷。

translations.literal: Authority and favor are his own; he looks upon the court with no regard.
translations.idiomatic: He monopolizes authority and favor and looks upon the court with contempt.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之法若是乎？

translations.literal: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?

sentences.zh: 祖宗朝，一切政事，臺省奏陳，部院題覆，撫按奉行，未聞閣臣有舉劾也。

translations.literal: In the age of the ancestors, for all government affairs the censorate memorialized, ministries and boards replied, and grand coordinators and touring inspectors carried out orders—one never heard of Grand Secretariat members conducting impeachments.
translations.idiomatic: Under the ancestors, for all government affairs the censorate memorialized, ministries and boards replied, and grand coordinators and touring inspectors carried out orders—one never heard of Grand Secretariat members conducting impeachments.

sentences.zh: 居正定令，撫按考成章奏，每具二冊，一送內閣，一送六科。

translations.literal: Juzheng fixed a regulation that grand coordinators' and touring inspectors' evaluation memorials should each be prepared in two copies, one sent to the Grand Secretariat and one to the Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng fixed a regulation that evaluation memorials from grand coordinators and touring inspectors should each be prepared in duplicate, one copy sent to the Grand Secretariat and one to the Six Offices.

sentences.zh: 撫按延遲，則部臣糾之。

translations.literal: If grand coordinators and touring inspectors were delayed, ministry officials impeached them.
translations.idiomatic: If grand coordinators or touring inspectors were delayed, ministry officials impeached them.

sentences.zh: 六部隱蔽，則科臣糾之。

translations.literal: If the Six Ministries concealed matters, censorial officials impeached them.
translations.idiomatic: If the Six Ministries concealed matters, censorial officials impeached them.

sentences.zh: 六科隱蔽，則內閣糾之。

translations.literal: If the Six Offices concealed matters, the Grand Secretariat impeached them.
translations.idiomatic: If the Six Offices concealed matters, the Grand Secretariat impeached them.

sentences.zh: 夫部院分理國事，科臣封駁奏章，舉劾，其職也。

translations.literal: Ministries and boards divide and manage state affairs; censorial officials seal, reject, and memorialize, and impeachment is their duty.
translations.idiomatic: Ministries and boards divide and manage state affairs; censorial officials seal, reject, and memorialize—and impeachment is their proper duty.

sentences.zh: 閣臣銜列翰林，止備顧問，從容論思而已。

translations.literal: Grand Secretariat members bear the title of Hanlin and are only to serve as advisers, discussing matters at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretariat members bear Hanlin titles and serve only as advisers, discussing matters at leisure.

sentences.zh: 居正創為是說，欲脅制科臣，拱手聽令。

translations.literal: Juzheng invented this doctrine in order to coerce censorial officials and make them fold their hands and obey orders.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng invented this doctrine to coerce censorial officials and make them fold their hands and obey his orders.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之法若是乎？

translations.literal: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?

sentences.zh: 至於按臣回道考察，茍非有大敗類者，常不舉行，蓋不欲重挫抑之。

translations.literal: As for touring inspectors returning and undergoing evaluation, unless there were grave failures they were usually not pursued, for the court did not wish to strike them down heavily.
translations.idiomatic: As for touring inspectors returning for evaluation, unless there were grave failures the inquiry was usually not pursued, for the court did not wish to strike them down heavily.

sentences.zh: 近日御史俞一貫以不聽指授，調之南京。

translations.literal: Recently Censor Yu Yiguan, for not obeying instructions, was transferred to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Censor Yu Yiguan, for not obeying instructions, was transferred to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 由是巡方短氣，莫敢展布，所憚獨科臣耳。

translations.literal: Hence touring inspectors of the regions lost spirit and none dared act freely; they feared only the censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Hence touring inspectors across the realm lost heart and none dared act freely; they feared only the censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 居正於科臣既啖之以遷轉之速，又恐之以考成之遲，誰肯舍其便利，甘彼齮龁，而盡死言事哉？

translations.literal: Juzheng both fed censorial officials with the speed of transfer and promotion and threatened them with the delay of performance evaluation—who would abandon such advantage, willingly endure his persecution, and speak to the death?
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng both tempted censorial officials with rapid promotion and threatened them with delayed performance evaluations—who would abandon such advantage, willingly endure his persecution, and speak to the death?

sentences.zh: 往年趙參魯以諫遷，猶曰外任也；

translations.literal: In former years Zhao Canlu was transferred for remonstrance, yet it was still called an outside appointment;
translations.idiomatic: In former years Zhao Canlu was transferred for remonstrance, yet it was still called an outside appointment;

sentences.zh: 余懋學以諫罷，猶曰禁錮也；

translations.literal: Yu Maoxue was dismissed for remonstrance, yet it was still called confinement;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Maoxue was dismissed for remonstrance, yet it was still called confinement;

sentences.zh: 今傅應禎則謫戍矣，又以應禎故，而及徐貞明、喬巖、李禎矣。

translations.literal: Now Fu Yingzhen has been banished to frontier service, and because of Yingzhen, Xu Zhenming, Qiao Yan, and Li Zhen have also been implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Now Fu Yingzhen has been banished to frontier service, and because of him Xu Zhenming, Qiao Yan, and Li Zhen have been implicated as well.

sentences.zh: 摧折言官，仇視正士。

translations.literal: He breaks remonstrating officials and treats upright men as enemies.
translations.idiomatic: He breaks remonstrating officials and treats upright men as enemies.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之法如是乎？

translations.literal: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how the laws of the ancestors run?

sentences.zh: 至若為固寵計，則獻白蓮白燕，致詔旨責讓，傳笑四方矣。

translations.literal: As for schemes to secure favor, he presented white lotus and white swallow, drawing an edict of reprimand and becoming a laughingstock throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: As for schemes to secure favor, he presented a white lotus and a white swallow, drawing an edict of reprimand and becoming a laughingstock throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 規利田宅，則誣遼王以重罪，而奪其府地，今武岡王又得罪矣。

translations.literal: To seize fields and houses for profit, he falsely charged the Prince of Liao with a grave crime and seized his estate lands; now the Prince of Wugang has also been charged.
translations.idiomatic: To seize fields and houses for profit, he falsely charged the Prince of Liao with a grave crime and seized his estate lands; now the Prince of Wugang has been charged as well.

sentences.zh: 為子弟謀舉鄉試，則許御史舒鰲以京堂，布政施堯臣以巡撫矣。

translations.literal: To secure his sons' success in the provincial examination, he promised Censor Shu Ao a capital post and Administration Commissioner Shi Yaochan a grand coordinator's post.
translations.idiomatic: To secure his sons' success in the provincial examination, he promised Censor Shu Ao a capital post and Administration Commissioner Shi Yaochan a grand coordinator's post.

sentences.zh: 起大第於江陵，費至十萬，制擬宮禁，遣錦衣官校監治，鄉郡之脂膏盡矣。

translations.literal: He raised a great mansion at Jiangling at a cost reaching one hundred thousand, its design rivaling the palace precincts, and sent brocade-clad guards to supervise construction until the fat of the home district was drained dry.
translations.idiomatic: He built a great mansion at Jiangling at a cost reaching one hundred thousand taels, its design rivaling the palace precincts, and sent brocade-clad guards to supervise construction until the wealth of his home district was drained dry.

sentences.zh: 惡黃州生儒議其子弟幸售，則假縣令他事窮治無遺矣。

translations.literal: Hating that Huangzhou student-scholars discussed how his sons had luckily passed, he used the county magistrate on other pretexts to investigate and punish without remainder.
translations.idiomatic: Angered that Huangzhou student-scholars discussed how his sons had luckily passed the examinations, he used the county magistrate on other pretexts to investigate and punish them without mercy.

sentences.zh: 編修李維楨偶談及其豪富，不旋踵即外斥矣。

translations.literal: Compiler Li Weizhen casually spoke of his enormous wealth, and before he could turn around he was expelled to an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: Compiler Li Weizhen casually mentioned his enormous wealth, and before he could turn around was expelled to an outside post.

sentences.zh: 蓋居正之貪，不在文吏而在武臣，不在內地而在邊鄙。

translations.literal: Juzheng's greed lay not among civil officials but among military officers, not in the interior but on the frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng's greed lay not among civil officials but among military officers, not in the interior but on the frontiers.

sentences.zh: 不然，輔政未幾，即富甲全楚，何由致之？

translations.literal: Otherwise, how could he, having assisted government only a short while, already be the richest man in all Chu—by what means did he obtain it?
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, how could he, having assisted government only a short while, already be the richest man in all Chu—by what means did he obtain such wealth?

sentences.zh: 宮室輿馬姬妾，奉禦同於王者，又何由致之？

translations.literal: Palaces, carriages, horses, and concubines, with attendants serving him like a king—by what means did he obtain these?
translations.idiomatic: Palaces, carriages, horses, and concubines, with attendants serving him like a king—by what means did he obtain these?

sentences.zh: 在朝臣工，莫不憤嘆，而無敢為陛下明言者，積威之劫也。

translations.literal: Among officials at court, none did not rage and sigh, yet none dared speak plainly to Your Majesty—such is the coercion of accumulated power.
translations.idiomatic: Every official at court raged and sighed, yet none dared speak plainly to Your Majesty—such is the coercion of accumulated power.

sentences.zh: 臣舉進士，居正為總裁。

translations.literal: Your servant passed the jinshi examination with Juzheng as chief examiner.
translations.idiomatic: I passed the jinshi examination with Juzheng as chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 臣任部曹，居正薦改御史。

translations.literal: When your servant served in a ministry bureau, Juzheng recommended changing him to censor.
translations.idiomatic: When I served in a ministry bureau, Juzheng recommended my transfer to censor.

sentences.zh: 臣受居正恩亦厚矣，而今敢訟言攻之者，君臣誼重，則私恩有不得而顧也。

translations.literal: Your servant has also received great favor from Juzheng, yet now dares openly to accuse and attack him because the bond between ruler and minister is weighty, and private favor cannot be considered.
translations.idiomatic: I have received great favor from Juzheng as well, yet I dare openly accuse him because the bond between ruler and minister outweighs private obligation.

sentences.zh: 願陛下察臣愚悃，抑損相權，毋俾僨事誤國，臣死且不朽。

translations.literal: Your servant wishes Your Majesty to discern his foolish sincerity, restrain the chief minister's power, and not let ruinous affairs harm the state—then even in death your servant will not perish.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to discern my sincere intent, restrain the chief minister's power, and not let ruinous affairs harm the state—then even in death I shall not perish.

sentences.zh: 疏上，居正怒甚，廷辯之，曰：「在令，巡按不得報軍功。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Juzheng was greatly angered and argued in court, saying, "By regulation, touring inspectors may not report military merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Juzheng was greatly angered and argued in court, saying, "By regulation, touring inspectors may not report military merit.

sentences.zh: 去年遼東大捷，臺違制妄奏，法應降謫。

translations.literal: Last year there was a great victory in Liaodong; Tai violated regulations and memorialized rashly; by law he should be demoted and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Last year there was a great victory in Liaodong; Tai violated regulations and memorialized rashly; by law he should be demoted and banished.

sentences.zh: 臣第請旨戒諭，而臺已不勝憤。

translations.literal: Your servant only requested an edict of admonition, yet Tai was already unable to contain his rage.
translations.idiomatic: I only requested an edict of admonition, yet Tai was already unable to contain his rage.

sentences.zh: 後傅應禎下獄，究詰黨與。

translations.literal: Later Fu Yingzhen was imprisoned and his faction was investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fu Yingzhen was imprisoned and his faction was investigated.

sentences.zh: 初不知臺與應禎同邑厚善，實有所主。

translations.literal: At first I did not know that Tai and Yingzhen were from the same district and on close terms, and that there was in fact a patron behind them.
translations.idiomatic: At first I did not know that Tai and Yingzhen were from the same district and on close terms, and that there was in fact a patron behind them.

sentences.zh: 乃妄自驚疑，遂不復顧藉，發憤於臣。

translations.literal: Then he rashly alarmed himself with suspicion, no longer showed regard, and vented his rage upon your servant.
translations.idiomatic: Then he rashly alarmed himself with suspicion, no longer showed regard, and vented his rage upon me.

sentences.zh: 且臺為臣所取士，二百年來無門生劾師長者，計惟一去謝之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Tai was a student your servant had passed in examination; in two hundred years there has been no student who impeached his teacher—his only plan can be to go once and apologize."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Tai was a student I had passed in examination; in two hundred years there has been no student who impeached his teacher—his only course can be to come once and apologize."

sentences.zh: 因辭政，伏地泣不肯起。

translations.literal: Thereupon he resigned his office, prostrated himself weeping and refused to rise.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he resigned his office, prostrated himself weeping, and refused to rise.

sentences.zh: 帝為降禦座手掖之，慰留再三。

translations.literal: The emperor descended from the imperial seat and raised him by the hand, repeatedly urging him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended from the imperial seat and raised him by the hand, repeatedly urging him to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 居正強諾，猶不出視事，帝遣司禮太監孫隆賫手敕宣諭，乃起。

translations.literal: Juzheng forced himself to assent but still did not attend to affairs; the emperor sent the Directorate of Ceremonial eunuch Sun Long with an imperial letter of instruction to announce and comfort him, and only then did he rise.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng forced himself to assent but still did not attend to affairs; the emperor sent the Directorate of Ceremonial eunuch Sun Long with an imperial letter of instruction, and only then did he resume office.

sentences.zh: 遂捕臺至京師，下詔獄，命廷杖百，遠戍。

translations.literal: Then Tai was arrested and brought to the capital, imprisoned in the imperial prison, ordered to receive one hundred blows in court, and banished to a distant post.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was then arrested and brought to the capital, imprisoned in the imperial prison, ordered to receive one hundred blows in court, and banished to a distant post.

sentences.zh: 居正陽具疏救，乃除名為民，而居正恨不已。

translations.literal: Juzheng outwardly submitted a memorial to save him, and Tai was only struck from the rolls and made a commoner, but Juzheng's hatred did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng outwardly submitted a memorial to save him, and Tai was only struck from the rolls and made a commoner, but Juzheng's hatred did not cease.

sentences.zh: 臺按遼東時，與巡撫張學顏不相得。

translations.literal: When Tai was inspecting Liaodong, he did not get along with Grand Coordinator Zhang Xueyan.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai was inspecting Liaodong, he did not get along with Grand Coordinator Zhang Xueyan.

sentences.zh: 至是學顏為戶部，誣臺私贖鍰，居正屬御史於應昌巡按遼東核之，而令王宗載巡撫江西，廉臺里中事。

translations.literal: At this time Xueyan was in the Ministry of Revenue and falsely charged Tai with privately redeeming fines; Juzheng directed Censor Yu Yingchang, touring inspector of Liaodong, to verify it, and ordered Wang Zongzai, grand coordinator of Jiangxi, to investigate Tai's affairs in his home district.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Xueyan was in the Ministry of Revenue and falsely charged Tai with privately redeeming fines; Juzheng directed Censor Yu Yingchang, touring inspector of Liaodong, to verify it, and ordered Wang Zongzai, grand coordinator of Jiangxi, to investigate Tai's affairs in his home district.

sentences.zh: 應昌、宗載等希居正意，實其事以聞，遂戍臺廣西。

translations.literal: Yingchang, Zongzai, and others conformed to Juzheng's wishes, substantiated the charges in their report, and Tai was banished to Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchang, Zongzai, and others conformed to Juzheng's wishes, substantiated the charges in their report, and Tai was banished to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 臺父震龍、弟國，俱坐罪。

translations.literal: Tai's father Zhenlong and his brother Guo were both punished for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Tai's father Zhenlong and his brother Guo were both punished as well.

sentences.zh: 臺至潯州未幾，飲於戍主所，歸而暴卒。

translations.literal: Not long after Tai reached Xunzhou, he drank at his guard commander's quarters, returned, and died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after Tai reached Xunzhou, he drank at his guard commander's quarters, returned home, and died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 是日居正亦卒。

translations.literal: On that same day Juzheng also died.
translations.idiomatic: On that same day Juzheng also died.

sentences.zh: 明年，御史江東之訟臺冤，劾宗載、應昌。

translations.literal: The next year Censor Jiang Dongzhi pleaded Tai's injustice and impeached Zongzai and Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Censor Jiang Dongzhi pleaded Tai's injustice and impeached Zongzai and Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 詔復臺官，罷宗載、應昌，下所司廉問。

translations.literal: An edict restored Tai's office, dismissed Zongzai and Yingchang, and ordered the relevant offices to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored Tai's office, dismissed Zongzai and Yingchang, and ordered the relevant offices to investigate.

sentences.zh: 南京給事中馮景隆因言遼東巡撫周詠與應昌共陷臺，應昌已罷，詠尚為薊遼總督，亦宜罷。

translations.literal: Nanjing Supervising Secretary Feng Jinglong stated that Liaodong Grand Coordinator Zhou Yong had joined Yingchang in framing Tai; Yingchang had already been dismissed, but Yong still served as supreme commander of Jizhou and Liaodong and should also be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Supervising Secretary Feng Jinglong stated that Liaodong Grand Coordinator Zhou Yong had joined Yingchang in framing Tai; Yingchang had already been dismissed, but Yong still served as supreme commander of Jizhou and Liaodong and should be dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 南京御史孫繼先亦發學顏陷臺罪。

translations.literal: Nanjing Censor Sun Jixian also exposed Xueyan's crime in framing Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing Censor Sun Jixian also exposed Xueyan's crime in framing Tai.

sentences.zh: 帝方向學顏。

translations.literal: The emperor was still inclined toward Xueyan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still inclined toward Xueyan.

sentences.zh: 以景隆疏中並劾李成梁，學顏為成梁訟。

translations.literal: Because Feng Jinglong's memorial also impeached Li Chengliang, Xueyan pleaded Chengliang's case.
translations.idiomatic: Because Feng Jinglong's memorial also impeached Li Chengliang, Xueyan pleaded Chengliang's case.

sentences.zh: 繼先又並劾學顏、成梁。

translations.literal: Sun Jixian again impeached both Xueyan and Chengliang.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jixian again impeached both Xueyan and Chengliang.

sentences.zh: 乃謫景隆薊州判官，繼先臨清州判官，置學顏不問。

translations.literal: Thereupon Feng Jinglong was demoted to assistant magistrate of Jizhou and Sun Jixian to assistant magistrate of Linqing, while Xueyan was left unpunished.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jinglong was demoted to assistant magistrate of Jizhou and Sun Jixian to assistant magistrate of Linqing, while Xueyan was left unpunished.

sentences.zh: 已而江西巡撫曹大埜、遼東巡撫李松，勘報宗載、應昌等朋比傾陷皆有狀。

translations.literal: Later Jiangxi Grand Coordinator Cao Daye and Liaodong Grand Coordinator Li Song investigated and reported that Zongzai, Yingchang, and others had formed a faction to frame Tai, all with substantiated facts.
translations.idiomatic: Later Jiangxi Grand Coordinator Cao Daye and Liaodong Grand Coordinator Li Song investigated and reported that Zongzai, Yingchang, and others had formed a faction to frame Tai, all with substantiated facts.

sentences.zh: 刑部以故入論，奏宗載等遣戍、除名、降黜有差。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishments judged them for intentional injury and memorialized that Zongzai and the others be banished, struck from the rolls, and demoted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Punishments judged them for intentional injury and memorialized that Zongzai and the others be banished, struck from the rolls, and demoted in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 贈臺光祿少卿，蔭一子。

translations.literal: Tai was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with one son given hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, with one son given hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，追謚毅思。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, he was posthumously given the temple name Yisi.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was posthumously given the temple name Yisi.

sentences.zh: 馮景隆，浙江山陰人。

translations.literal: Feng Jinglong was a man of Shanyin in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jinglong was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 嘗訟趙世卿冤，且請召張位、習孔教，申救御史魏允貞，至是謫官。

translations.literal: He had once pleaded Zhao Shiqing's injustice and also requested the recall of Zhang Wei and Xi Kongjiao and interceded for Censor Wei Yunzhen; now he was demoted.
translations.idiomatic: He had once pleaded Zhao Shiqing's injustice, requested the recall of Zhang Wei and Xi Kongjiao, and interceded for Censor Wei Yunzhen; now he was demoted.

sentences.zh: 後量移南陽推官。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to judicial assistant at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred to judicial assistant at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 孫繼先，字胤甫，盂人。

translations.literal: Sun Jixian, styled Yinfu, was a man of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jixian, styled Yinfu, was a native of Yu.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Longqing.

sentences.zh: 居正既敗，繼先請召吳中行、趙用賢、艾穆、沈思孝、鄒元標並及余懋學、趙應元、傅應禎、朱鴻謨、孟一脈、王用汲。

translations.literal: After Juzheng's fall, Jixian requested the recall of Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, Ai Mu, Shen Sixiao, Zou Yuanbiao, and also Yu Maoxue, Zhao Yingyuan, Fu Yingzhen, Zhu Hongmo, Meng Yimai, and Wang Yongji.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's fall, Jixian requested the recall of Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, Ai Mu, Shen Sixiao, Zou Yuanbiao, and also Yu Maoxue, Zhao Yingyuan, Fu Yingzhen, Zhu Hongmo, Meng Yimai, and Wang Yongji.

sentences.zh: 又薦魏學曾、宋糸熏、張嶽、毛綱、胡執禮、王錫爵、賈三近、溫純、曹科、陳有年、朱光宇、趙參魯等諸人。

translations.literal: He also recommended Wei Xuezeng, Song Xun, Zhang Yue, Mao Gang, Hu Zhili, Wang Xijue, Jia Sanjin, Wen Chun, Cao Ke, Chen Younian, Zhu Guangyu, Zhao Canlu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Wei Xuezeng, Song Xun, Zhang Yue, Mao Gang, Hu Zhili, Wang Xijue, Jia Sanjin, Wen Chun, Cao Ke, Chen Younian, Zhu Guangyu, Zhao Canlu, and others.

sentences.zh: 既坐謫，終南京吏部主事。

translations.literal: Having been punished with demotion, he ended as principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Having been punished with demotion, he ended his career as principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 傅應禎，字公善，安福人。

translations.literal: Fu Yingzhen, styled Gongshan, was a man of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Yingzhen, styled Gongshan, was a native of Anfu.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Longqing.

sentences.zh: 除零陵知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Lingling.

sentences.zh: 殲洞庭劇寇，論殺祁陽巨猾，民賴以安。

translations.literal: He destroyed fierce bandits on Dongting Lake and sentenced to death a great villain of Qiyang; the people relied on him for peace.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed fierce bandits on Dongting Lake and sentenced to death a great villain of Qiyang; the people relied on him for peace.

sentences.zh: 調知溧水。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Lishui.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Lishui.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三年，征授御史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Wanli he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Wanli he was summoned and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 張居正當國，應禎其門生也，有所感憤，疏陳重君德、蘇民困、開言路三事，言：

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng held power, Yingzhen was his student; stirred by indignation, he memorialized on three matters—honoring the ruler's virtue, relieving the people's distress, and opening the path of remonstrance—saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng held power, Yingzhen was his student; stirred by indignation, he memorialized on three matters—honoring the ruler's virtue, relieving the people's distress, and opening the path of remonstrance—saying:

sentences.zh: 邇者雷震端門獸吻，京師及四方地震疊告，曾未聞發詔修省，豈真以天變不足畏耶？

translations.literal: Recently thunder shook the beast finials of the Gate of Correct Deportment, and earthquakes in the capital and the four directions were reported in succession, yet no edict of self-examination was heard—does Your Majesty truly hold that heavenly changes are not to be feared?
translations.idiomatic: Recently thunder shook the beast finials of the Gate of Correct Deportment, and earthquakes in the capital and throughout the realm were reported in succession, yet no edict of self-examination was issued—does Your Majesty truly hold that heavenly changes are not to be feared?

sentences.zh: 真定抽分中使，本非舊典，正統間嘗暫行之，先帝納李芳言，已詔罷遣，而陛下顧欲踵行失德之事，豈真以祖宗不足法耶？

translations.literal: The eunuch commissioners for levy at Zhending were never an old institution; they were briefly employed in the Zhengtong reign, and the late emperor, accepting Li Fang's advice, had already ordered them dismissed—yet Your Majesty wishes to follow unworthy precedents; does Your Majesty truly hold that the ancestors are not to be followed?
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch commissioners for levy at Zhending were never an established institution; they were briefly employed in the Zhengtong reign, and the late emperor, accepting Li Fang's advice, had already ordered them dismissed—yet Your Majesty wishes to follow unworthy precedents; does Your Majesty truly hold that the ancestors are not to be followed?

sentences.zh: 給事中朱東光奏陳保治，初非折檻解衣者比，乃竟留中不報，豈真以人言不足恤耶？

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhu Dongguang memorialized on preserving order; he was no breaker of the balustrade or stripper of robes, yet his memorial was kept at court and not reported—does Your Majesty truly hold that human speech is not to be heeded?
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhu Dongguang memorialized on preserving order; he was no desperate remonstrator, yet his memorial was kept at court and not reported—does Your Majesty truly hold that human speech is not to be heeded?

sentences.zh: 此三不足者，王安石以之誤宋，不可不深戒也。

translations.literal: These three 'not to be feared' or 'not to be followed' or 'not to be heeded'—Wang Anshi used them to mislead Song; they must be deeply taken as warning.
translations.idiomatic: These three attitudes—Wang Anshi used them to mislead Song; they must be deeply taken as warning.

sentences.zh: 陛下登極初，自隆慶改元以前逋租，悉賜蠲除，四年以前免三征七，恩至渥也。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, all arrears of rent before the Longqing reign change were entirely remitted, and for four years prior three parts in seven were exempted—grace reached the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, all arrears of rent before the Longqing reign change were entirely remitted, and for four years prior three parts in seven were exempted—grace reached the utmost.

sentences.zh: 乃上軫恤已至，而下延玩自如，曾未有擔負相屬者，何哉？

translations.literal: Yet though compassion from above had arrived, below they delayed and played as before, and never were burdens passed on—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yet though compassion from above had arrived, below officials delayed and played as before, and burdens were never passed upward—why?

sentences.zh: 小民一歲之入，僅足給一歲，無遺力以償負也。

translations.literal: The common people's yearly income barely suffices for one year; they have no surplus strength to repay debts.
translations.idiomatic: The common people's yearly income barely suffices for one year; they have no surplus strength to repay debts.

sentences.zh: 近乃定輸不及額者，按撫聽糾，郡縣聽調。

translations.literal: Recently it was fixed that where payment fell short of quota, grand coordinators and touring inspectors might impeach, and prefectures and counties might be transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Recently it was fixed that where payment fell short of quota, grand coordinators and touring inspectors might impeach, and prefectures and counties might be transferred.

sentences.zh: 諸臣畏譴，督趣倍嚴。

translations.literal: Officials feared punishment and pressed collection twice as harshly.
translations.idiomatic: Officials feared punishment and pressed collection twice as harshly.

sentences.zh: 致流離接踵，怨咨愁嘆，上徹於天。

translations.literal: This caused displacement to follow in succession, resentment and lament to reach heaven.
translations.idiomatic: This caused displacement to follow in succession, resentment and lament to reach heaven.

sentences.zh: 是豈太平之象，陛下所樂聞者哉？

translations.literal: Is this the image of great peace that Your Majesty delights to hear?
translations.idiomatic: Is this the image of great peace that Your Majesty delights to hear?

sentences.zh: 請下明詔，自非官吏幹沒，並曠然除之。

translations.literal: Your servant begs that a clear edict be issued: except where officials have embezzled, all debts be broadly remitted.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that a clear edict be issued: except where officials have embezzled, all debts be broadly remitted.

sentences.zh: 民困既蘇，則災沴自弭。

translations.literal: Once the people's distress is relieved, calamities will naturally cease.
translations.idiomatic: Once the people's distress is relieved, calamities will naturally cease.

sentences.zh: 陛下登極初，召用直臣石星、李已，臣工無不慶幸。

translations.literal: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, upright ministers Shi Xing and Li Yi were summoned and employed; officials were without exception rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty first ascended the throne, upright ministers Shi Xing and Li Yi were summoned and employed; officials rejoiced without exception.

sentences.zh: 近則趙參魯糾中涓而謫為典史，余懋學陳時政而錮之終身，他如胡執禮、裴應章、侯於趙、趙煥等封事累上，一切置之，如初政何？

translations.literal: Recently Zhao Canlu impeached a palace eunuch and was demoted to record keeper; Yu Maoxue stated current policy and was confined for life; others such as Hu Zhili, Pei Yingzhang, Hou Yuzhao, and Zhao Huan submitted sealed memorials repeatedly, all set aside—how does this compare with the early reign?
translations.idiomatic: Recently Zhao Canlu impeached a palace eunuch and was demoted to record keeper; Yu Maoxue stated current policy and was confined for life; others such as Hu Zhili, Pei Yingzhang, Hou Yuzhao, and Zhao Huan submitted sealed memorials repeatedly, all set aside—how does this compare with the early reign?

sentences.zh: 臣請擢參魯京職，還懋學故官，為人臣進言者勸。

translations.literal: Your servant begs to promote Canlu to a capital post and restore Maoxue to his former office, to encourage those who speak as ministers.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to promote Canlu to a capital post and restore Maoxue to his former office, to encourage those who speak as ministers.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，居正以疏中王安石語侵己，大怒，調旨切責；

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Juzheng, because the Wang Anshi language in the memorial offended him, was greatly angered and had an edict drafted to rebuke him sharply;
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Juzheng, offended by the Wang Anshi language in the memorial, was greatly angered and had an edict drafted to rebuke him sharply;

sentences.zh: 以其詞及懋學，執下詔獄，窮治黨與。

translations.literal: because the wording touched on Maoxue, he had Yingzhen seized and imprisoned in the imperial prison and thoroughly investigated his faction.
translations.idiomatic: because the wording touched on Maoxue, he had Yingzhen seized and imprisoned in the imperial prison and thoroughly investigated his faction.

sentences.zh: 應禎瀕死無所承，乃謫戍定海。

translations.literal: Yingzhen, on the verge of death, confessed to nothing, and was banished to garrison service at Dinghai.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen, on the verge of death, confessed to nothing and was banished to garrison service at Dinghai.

sentences.zh: 給事中嚴用和、御史劉天衢等疏救，不聽。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yan Yonghe, Censor Liu Tianqu, and others memorialized to save him; the emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yan Yonghe, Censor Liu Tianqu, and others memorialized to save him; the emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 方應禎下獄，給事中徐貞明偕御史李禎、喬巖入視之。

translations.literal: When Yingzhen was imprisoned, Supervising Secretary Xu Zhenming together with Censors Li Zhen and Qiao Yan entered to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzhen was imprisoned, Supervising Secretary Xu Zhenming together with Censors Li Zhen and Qiao Yan entered to visit him.

sentences.zh: 錦衣帥余蔭以聞，三人亦坐謫。

translations.literal: The brocade-clad guard commander Yu Yin reported it, and the three were also punished with demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The brocade-clad guard commander Yu Yin reported it, and the three were also punished with demotion.

sentences.zh: 十一年，用御史孫繼先言，召復官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, on the word of Censor Sun Jixian, he was recalled and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year, on the word of Censor Sun Jixian, he was recalled and restored to office.

sentences.zh: 帝將幸昌平閱壽宮，而薊鎮告警，應禎止帝勿行，且陳邊備甚悉。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to visit Changping to inspect the mausoleum, but Jizhou garrison reported alarm; Yingzhen urged the emperor not to go and also stated frontier defense in great detail.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to visit Changping to inspect the mausoleum, but the Jizhou garrison reported alarm; Yingzhen urged the emperor not to go and stated frontier defense in great detail.

sentences.zh: 優詔答之。

translations.literal: A gracious edict answered him.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict answered him.

sentences.zh: 俄擢南京大理寺丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to vice director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to vice director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 將行，奏薦海內知名士三十七人。

translations.literal: Before departing he memorialized recommending thirty-seven renowned scholars throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Before departing he memorialized recommending thirty-seven renowned scholars throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 尋移疾歸，三年而卒。

translations.literal: Soon he pleaded illness and returned home; three years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he pleaded illness and returned home; three years later he died.

sentences.zh: 贈本寺右少卿。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of that court.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of that court.

sentences.zh: 應禎與同邑劉臺同舉進士，為御史，同忤居正得禍，鄉人並祠祀之。

translations.literal: Yingzhen and Liu Tai of the same district passed the jinshi together, served as censors, and alike offended Juzheng and suffered disaster; fellow townsmen jointly enshrined them.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen and Liu Tai of the same district passed the jinshi together, served as censors, and alike offended Juzheng and suffered disaster; fellow townsmen jointly enshrined them.

sentences.zh: 王用汲，字明受，晉江人。

translations.literal: Wang Yongji, styled Mingshou, was a man of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yongji, styled Mingshou, was a native of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 為諸生時，郡被倭，客兵橫市中。

translations.literal: When he was a student, the prefecture suffered Japanese raids and mercenary troops rampaged in the market.
translations.idiomatic: When he was a student, the prefecture suffered Japanese raids and mercenary troops rampaged in the market.

sentences.zh: 會御史按部至，用汲言狀。

translations.literal: When a censor arrived on inspection tour, Yongji reported the situation.
translations.idiomatic: When a censor arrived on inspection tour, Yongji reported the situation.

sentences.zh: 知府曰：「此何與諸生事？」

translations.literal: The prefect said, "What has this to do with a student's affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: The prefect said, "What has this to do with a student's affairs?"

sentences.zh: 用汲曰：「範希文秀才時，以天下為己任，矧鄉井之禍乃不關諸生耶？」

translations.literal: Yongji said, "When Fan Xiwen was a student he took the realm as his own charge—how can the calamity of one's home district not concern a student?"
translations.idiomatic: Yongji said, "When Fan Xiwen was a student he took the realm as his own charge—how can the calamity of one's home district not concern a student?"

sentences.zh: 舉隆慶二年進士，授淮安推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in the second year of Longqing and was appointed judicial assistant at Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the second year of Longqing and was appointed judicial assistant at Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 稍遷常德同知，入為戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to vice prefect of Changde and entered service as a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually transferred to vice prefect of Changde and entered service as a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 萬歷六年，首輔張居正歸葬其親，湖廣諸司畢會。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Wanli, Chief Minister Zhang Juzheng returned to bury his parent; all offices of Huguang assembled.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wanli, Chief Minister Zhang Juzheng returned to bury his parent; all offices of Huguang assembled.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史趙應元獨不往，居正嗛之。

translations.literal: Touring Inspector Zhao Yingyuan alone did not go; Juzheng resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Inspector Zhao Yingyuan alone did not go; Juzheng resented him.

sentences.zh: 及應元事竣得代，即以病請。

translations.literal: When Yingyuan finished his term and was to be replaced, he immediately pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingyuan finished his term and was to be replaced, he immediately pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 僉都御史王篆者，居正客也，素憾應元，且迎合居正意，屬都御史陳炌劾應元規避，遂除名。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhuan was Juzheng's client, had long resented Yingyuan, and moreover conformed to Juzheng's wishes, directing Censor-in-Chief Chen Can to impeach Yingyuan for evasion; he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Zhuan was Juzheng's client, had long resented Yingyuan, and conformed to Juzheng's wishes, directing Censor-in-Chief Chen Can to impeach Yingyuan for evasion; he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 用汲不勝憤，乃上言：

translations.literal: Yongji, unable to contain his anger, then memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yongji, unable to contain his anger, then memorialized, saying:

sentences.zh: 御史應元以不會葬得罪輔臣，遂為都御史炌所論，坐托疾欺罔削籍，臣竊恨之。

translations.literal: Censor Yingyuan offended the chief minister by not attending the funeral and was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Can, punished for feigning illness and deception and struck from the rolls—your servant privately resents this.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yingyuan offended the chief minister by not attending the funeral and was impeached by Censor-in-Chief Can, punished for feigning illness and deception and struck from the rolls—I resent this deeply.

sentences.zh: 夫疾病人所時有，今在廷大小諸臣，曾以病請者何限。

translations.literal: Illness is something all people sometimes have; among great and small officials at court today, how many have pleaded illness?
translations.idiomatic: Illness is something all people sometimes have; among great and small officials at court today, how many have pleaded illness?

sentences.zh: 御史陸萬鐘、劉光國、陳用賓皆以巡方事訖引疾，與應元不異也，炌何不並劾之？

translations.literal: Censors Lu Wanzhong, Liu Guangguo, and Chen Yongbin all pleaded illness when their regional tours ended, no different from Yingyuan—why did Can not impeach them all?
translations.idiomatic: Censors Lu Wanzhong, Liu Guangguo, and Chen Yongbin all pleaded illness when their regional tours ended, no different from Yingyuan—why did Can not impeach them all?

sentences.zh: 即炌當世宗朝，亦養病十余年。

translations.literal: Can himself, in the Shizong reign, also nursed illness for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Can himself, in the Shizong reign, also nursed illness for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 後夤緣攀附，驟列要津。

translations.literal: Later he climbed by connections and was suddenly placed in a key post.
translations.idiomatic: Later he climbed by connections and was suddenly placed in a key post.

sentences.zh: 以退為進，宜莫如炌。

translations.literal: Using withdrawal as advance, none should be like Can.
translations.idiomatic: Using withdrawal as advance, none should be like Can.

sentences.zh: 己則行之，而反以責人，何以服天下？

translations.literal: He does it himself yet blames others—how can he win the realm?
translations.idiomatic: He does it himself yet blames others—how can he win the realm?

sentences.zh: 陛下但見炌論劾應元，以為恣情趨避，罪當罷斥。

translations.literal: Your Majesty only saw Can impeach Yingyuan and thought him willfully evasive, deserving dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty only saw Can impeach Yingyuan and thought him willfully evasive, deserving dismissal.

sentences.zh: 至其意所從來，陛下何由知之。

translations.literal: As for whence his intent came, how could Your Majesty know?
translations.idiomatic: As for whence his intent came, how could Your Majesty know?

sentences.zh: 如昨歲星變考察，將以弭災也，而所挫抑者，半不附宰臣之人。

translations.literal: As in last year's evaluation after the stellar anomaly, meant to quell calamity—yet half of those struck down were men not attached to the chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: As in last year's evaluation after the stellar anomaly, meant to quell calamity—yet half of those struck down were men not attached to the chief minister.

sentences.zh: 如翰林習孔教，則以鄒元標之故；

translations.literal: Hanlin Compiler Xi Kongjiao, because of Zou Yuanbiao;
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Compiler Xi Kongjiao, because of Zou Yuanbiao;

sentences.zh: 禮部張程，則以劉臺之故；

translations.literal: Ministry of Rites Zhang Cheng, because of Liu Tai;
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Rites Zhang Cheng, because of Liu Tai;

sentences.zh: 刑部浮躁獨多於他部，則以艾穆、沈思孝而推戈；

translations.literal: the Ministry of Punishments alone had many judged frivolous beyond other ministries, because of Ai Mu and Shen Sixiao the spear was turned;
translations.idiomatic: the Ministry of Punishments alone had many judged frivolous beyond other ministries, because of Ai Mu and Shen Sixiao the spear was turned;

sentences.zh: 考後劣轉趙誌臯，又以吳中行、趙用賢而遷怒。

translations.literal: after evaluation Zhao Zhigao was transferred for inferiority, again from anger at Wu Zhongxing and Zhao Yongxian.
translations.idiomatic: after evaluation Zhao Zhigao was transferred for inferiority, again from anger at Wu Zhongxing and Zhao Yongxian.

sentences.zh: 蓋能得輔臣之心，則雖屢經論列之潘晟，且得以不次蒙恩；

translations.literal: For those who could win the chief minister's heart, even Pan Sheng, though repeatedly impeached, could receive extraordinary favor;
translations.idiomatic: For those who could win the chief minister's heart, even Pan Sheng, though repeatedly impeached, could receive extraordinary favor;

sentences.zh: 茍失輔臣之心，則雖素負才名之張嶽，難免以不及論調。

translations.literal: if they lost the chief minister's heart, even Zhang Yue, though long famed for talent, could not escape transfer on grounds of inadequacy.
translations.idiomatic: if they lost the chief minister's heart, even Zhang Yue, though long famed for talent, could not escape transfer on grounds of inadequacy.

sentences.zh: 臣不意陛下省災塞咎之舉，僅為宰臣酬恩報怨之私。

translations.literal: Your servant did not expect that Your Majesty's measures to examine calamity and block fault would serve only the chief minister's private settling of favors and grudges.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect that Your Majesty's measures to examine calamity and block fault would serve only the chief minister's private settling of favors and grudges.

sentences.zh: 且凡附宰臣者，亦各藉以酬其私，可不為太息矣哉！

translations.literal: Moreover, all who attached to the chief minister likewise used this to settle their private scores—can one not sigh deeply!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, all who attached to the chief minister likewise used this to settle their private scores—can one not sigh deeply!

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：「逢君之惡其罪大。」

translations.literal: Mencius said, "To meet the ruler's evil is a great crime.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, "To meet the ruler's evil is a great crime.

sentences.zh: 臣則謂逢相之惡其罪更大也。

translations.literal: Your servant would say that to meet the chief minister's evil is a crime even greater still.
translations.idiomatic: I would say that flattering the chief minister's wrongdoing is an even greater crime.

sentences.zh: 陛下天縱聖明，從諫勿咈。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is heaven-endowed and sagely clear, accepting remonstrance and not rejecting it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is endowed with natural sagacity and welcomes remonstrance without turning it aside.

sentences.zh: 諸臣熟知其然，爭欲碎首批鱗以自見。

translations.literal: The officials all know this well and vie to smash head and first scales to show themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The officials all know this, and each races to risk his life in remonstrance to make himself known.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲織錦綺，則撫臣、按臣言之；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wished to weave brocade and silk, then touring and investigating censors spoke of it;
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty wanted brocades and silks, touring and investigating censors raised the matter;

sentences.zh: 欲采珍異，則部臣、科臣言之；

translations.literal: if to gather rare and exotic goods, then ministry officials and supervising secretaries spoke;
translations.idiomatic: when you sought rare curiosities, ministry and supervising-secretariat officials spoke up;

sentences.zh: 欲取太倉光祿，則臺臣、科臣又言之。

translations.literal: if to take from the Granary and the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then censorate and supervising secretariat officials again spoke.
translations.idiomatic: when you drew on the state granaries and the Court of Imperial Entertainments, censorate and supervising-secretariat officials spoke again.

sentences.zh: 陛下悉見嘉納，或遂停止，或不為例。

translations.literal: Your Majesty fully saw, praised, and accepted them, sometimes stopping forthwith, sometimes not making a precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty accepted their advice in full—sometimes halting the matter outright, sometimes refusing to set a precedent.

sentences.zh: 至若輔臣意之所向，不論是否，無敢一言以正其非，且有先意結其歡，望風張其焰者，是臣所謂逢也。

translations.literal: As for where the chief minister's intent inclined, regardless of right or wrong, none dared speak one word to correct his error, and some anticipated his wish to win his favor and fanned his flame wherever they sensed the wind—this is what your servant calls flattering.
translations.idiomatic: But where the chief minister's will pointed, right or wrong, no one dared speak to correct him; some anticipated his wishes to win his favor and fanned his arrogance wherever they sensed his mood—this is what I mean by flattery.

sentences.zh: 今大臣未有不逢相之惡者，炌特其較著者爾。

translations.literal: Today among great ministers none fail to meet the chief minister's evil; Can is only the more conspicuous case.
translations.idiomatic: Today there is hardly a senior minister who does not pander to the chief minister's wishes; Can is merely the most conspicuous example.

sentences.zh: 以臣觀之，天下無事不私，無人不私，獨陛下一人公耳。

translations.literal: In your servant's view, under heaven nothing is without private interest and no man is without private interest—Your Majesty alone is public-minded.
translations.idiomatic: In my view, nothing under heaven is free of private interest, and no man is free of it—Your Majesty alone stands for the public good.

sentences.zh: 陛下又不躬自聽斷，而委政於眾所阿奉之大臣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty furthermore does not personally hear and decide, but entrusts government to the great minister whom all flatter.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty does not hear and decide cases yourself, but delegates authority to the minister whom all fawn upon.

sentences.zh: 大臣益得成其私而無所顧忌，小臣益苦行私而無所訴告，是驅天下而使之奔走乎私門矣。

translations.literal: The great minister increasingly achieves his private ends without fear; small officials increasingly bitterly practice private ends with none to whom they may appeal—this drives all under heaven to run to private gates.
translations.idiomatic: The senior minister grows bolder in pursuing his private ends; junior officials follow suit with no one to whom they can appeal—thus the whole realm is driven to scramble at private doorways.

sentences.zh: 陛下何不日取庶政而勤習之，內外章奏躬自省覽，先以意可否焉，然後宣付輔臣，俾之商榷。

translations.literal: Why does Your Majesty not daily take the various affairs of state and study them diligently, personally examine memorials from within and without, first form approval or rejection in your own mind, then announce and entrust them to the chief minister for deliberation?
translations.idiomatic: Why not take up the daily business of government and study it diligently, read memorials from within and without court yourself, form your own judgment first, and only then hand matters to the chief minister for deliberation?

sentences.zh: 閱習既久，智慮益弘，幾微隱伏之間，自無逃於天鑒。

translations.literal: Once review and study have lasted long, wisdom and consideration grow broader; in the minutest and hidden recesses, nothing escapes Heaven's scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: With long practice your discernment will broaden, and nothing in the subtlest hidden matters will escape your judgment.

sentences.zh: 夫威福者，陛下所當自出；

translations.literal: Authority and favor—Your Majesty ought to issue them yourself;
translations.idiomatic: The power to reward and punish is yours to wield;

sentences.zh: 乾綱者，陛下所當獨攬。

translations.literal: the celestial regalia—Your Majesty ought to hold it alone.
translations.idiomatic: the imperial prerogative is yours alone to hold.

sentences.zh: 寄之於人，不謂之旁落，則謂之倒持。

translations.literal: Entrusting them to others, if one does not call it power slipping to the side, one calls it holding the sword by the blade.
translations.idiomatic: To entrust them to others is either to let authority slip from your hands or to hand someone the hilt while the blade points back at you.

sentences.zh: 政柄一移，積重難返，此又臣所日夜深慮，不獨為應元一事已也。

translations.literal: Once the handle of government shifts, weight accumulates and return is hard—this too is what your servant deeply worries day and night, not only over the Yingyuan affair.
translations.idiomatic: Once power shifts, it gathers weight and cannot easily be reclaimed—this too weighs on me day and night, and not only because of the Yingyuan case.

sentences.zh: 疏入，居正大怒，欲下獄廷杖。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, Juzheng was greatly enraged and wished to send him to prison and beat him at court.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Juzheng was furious and wanted him imprisoned and beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 會次輔呂調陽在告，張四維擬削用汲籍，帝從之。

translations.literal: As it happened the second chief minister Lü Diaoyang was on leave; Zhang Siwei proposed striking Yongji from the rolls; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: As it happened the second chief minister Lü Diaoyang was on leave; Zhang Siwei proposed striking Yongji from the register, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 居正以罪輕，移怒四維，厲色待之者累日。

translations.literal: Juzheng, thinking the punishment too light, shifted his anger to Siwei and received him with stern countenance for many days.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng, deeming the penalty too mild, turned his anger on Siwei and treated him with a harsh face for days on end.

sentences.zh: 用汲歸，屏居郭外，布衣講授，足不賤城市。

translations.literal: Yongji returned home, lived in seclusion beyond the walls, taught in plain cloth, and his feet did not demean themselves by entering the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji went home, lived in seclusion outside the walls, taught in plain clothes, and would not set foot in the city.

sentences.zh: 居正死，起補刑部。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, he was recalled to fill a post in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death he was recalled to a post in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 未上，擢廣東僉事。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post, he was promoted to vice commissioner of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Before he assumed the post he was promoted to vice commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 尋召為尚寶卿，進大理少卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and advanced to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 會法司議胡槚、龍宗武殺吳仕期獄，傅以謫戍。

translations.literal: When the judiciary deliberated the case of Hu Zhu and Long Zongwu killing Wu Shiqi, they proposed banishment to garrison service.
translations.idiomatic: When the judiciary reviewed the case of Hu Zhu and Long Zongwu in the killing of Wu Shiqi, they proposed exile to frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 用汲駁奏曰：「按律，刑部及大小官吏，不依法律、聽從上司主使、出入人罪者，罪如之。

translations.literal: Yongji rebutted in a memorial, saying: "According to the code, officials of the Ministry of Punishments and all great and small officers who, not following the law, obey a superior's instigation to warp guilt in or out, are punished as the principal offense.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji rebutted in a memorial: "Under the code, officials of the Ministry of Punishments and all officers great and small who, disregarding the law, follow a superior's orders to manipulate guilt are punished as for the principal offense.

sentences.zh: 蓋謂如上文，罪斬、妻子為奴、財產入官之律也。

translations.literal: This means, as in the article above, the statute of decapitation, wives and children enslaved, and property confiscated to the state.
translations.idiomatic: That is, the statute above prescribing decapitation, enslavement of wife and children, and confiscation of property to the state.

sentences.zh: 仕期之死，槚非主使者乎？

translations.literal: In Shiqi's death, was Zhu not the instigator?
translations.idiomatic: In Shiqi's death, was Zhu not the one who instigated it?

sentences.zh: 宗武非聽上司主使者乎？

translations.literal: Was Zongwu not one who obeyed a superior's instigation?
translations.idiomatic: Did Zongwu not follow a superior's orders?

sentences.zh: 今僅謫戍，不知所遵何律也。」

translations.literal: Now they are merely banished to garrison service—I do not know what statute is being followed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now they receive only banishment to the frontier—I do not know which statute that follows.

sentences.zh: 上欲用用汲言，閣臣申時行等謂仕期自斃，宜減等，獄遂定。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to adopt Yongji's argument; Grand Secretaries Shen Shixing and others said Shiqi had died by his own hand and the penalty should be reduced; the case was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to follow Yongji's argument, but Grand Secretaries Shen Shixing and others said Shiqi had died by his own hand and the penalty should be reduced; the case was closed on that basis.

sentences.zh: 尋遷順天府尹。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 歷南京刑部尚書，致仕。

translations.literal: He served through the post of Minister of Punishments at Nanjing and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of Punishments at Nanjing and then retired.

sentences.zh: 用汲為人剛正，遇事敢為。

translations.literal: Yongji as a man was upright and firm, daring to act when matters arose.
translations.idiomatic: Yongji was upright and resolute, daring to act when the occasion demanded.

sentences.zh: 自尹京後，累遷皆在南，以強直故也。

translations.literal: From the time he governed the capital onward, his successive promotions were all in the south, because of his forceful uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: After he governed the capital, every further promotion kept him in the south—on account of his uncompromising character.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保，謚恭質。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Gongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Gongzhi.

sentences.zh: 吳中行，字子道，武進人。

translations.literal: Wu Zhongxing, styled Zidao, was a man of Wujin.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhongxing, styled Zidao, was a native of Wujin.

sentences.zh: 父性，兄可行，皆進士。

translations.literal: His father Xing and elder brother Kexing were both jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xing and elder brother Kexing had both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 性，尚寶丞。

translations.literal: Xing was deputy director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Xing served as deputy director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 可行，檢討。

translations.literal: Kexing was a reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Kexing was a reviser in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 中行甫冠，舉鄉試，性誡無躁進，遂不赴會試。

translations.literal: Zhongxing had just come of age and passed the provincial examination; Xing warned him not to rush advancement, so he did not attend the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing had just come of age when he passed the provincial examination; Xing warned him against hasty advancement, so he did not sit for the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 隆慶五年成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Longqing he became jinshi, was selected as a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Longqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 大學士張居正，中行座主也。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng was Zhongxing's examination patron.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng had been Zhongxing's chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年，居正遭父喪，奪情視事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli, Juzheng suffered his father's death and was granted leave from mourning to continue in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Wanli, Juzheng's father died; he was released from mourning obligations and continued in office.

sentences.zh: 御史曾士楚、吏科都給事中陳三謨倡疏奏留，舉朝和之，中行獨憤。

translations.literal: Censor Zeng Shichu and supervising secretary Chen Sanmo of the Ministry of Personnel led memorials to keep him; the whole court chimed in; Zhongxing alone was indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zeng Shichu and supervising secretary Chen Sanmo of the Ministry of Personnel led memorials asking him to stay; the whole court echoed them; Zhongxing alone was outraged.

sentences.zh: 適彗出西南，長竟天，詔百官修省，中行乃首上疏曰：「居正父子異地分暌，音容不接者十有九年。

translations.literal: Just then a comet appeared in the southwest and stretched across the sky; an edict ordered all officials to cultivate repentance; Zhongxing was first to submit a memorial, saying: "Between Juzheng and his father, separated in different places, voice and countenance have not met for nineteen years.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a comet appeared in the southwest and stretched across the heavens; an edict ordered all officials to examine themselves; Zhongxing was the first to submit a memorial, saying: "Father and son, Juzheng and his father, have lived apart; they have not heard each other's voice or seen each other's face for nineteen years.

sentences.zh: 一旦長棄數千里外，陛下不使匍匐星奔，憑棺一慟，必欲其違心抑情，銜哀茹痛於廟堂之上，而責以訏謨遠猷，調元熙載，豈情也哉！

translations.literal: In one morning he is long abandoned thousands of li away; Your Majesty does not let him crawl and run like a star, lean on the coffin and wail once; you must have him go against heart and suppress feeling, hold grief and endure pain in the hall of state, and charge him with grand counsel and distant plans, harmonizing the primal and glorifying the age—how is this fitting to feeling!
translations.idiomatic: Now his father lies dead thousands of li away, yet Your Majesty will not let him rush home on hands and knees to mourn at the coffin; you insist that he stifle his grief and serve in the hall of state, and still demand of him grand strategy and the work of governing the realm—can this be human?

sentences.zh: 居正每自言謹守聖賢義理，祖宗法度。

translations.literal: Juzheng often said himself that he strictly upheld the principles of sages and worthies and the regulations of the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng often declares that he strictly upholds the teachings of the sages and the regulations of the ancestors.

sentences.zh: 宰我欲短喪，子曰：『予有三年之愛於其父母乎？』

translations.literal: Zai Wo wished to shorten mourning; the Master said, "Did the Master have three years of love for his parents?
translations.idiomatic: When Zai Wo wished to shorten mourning, the Master said, "Did you have three years of love for your parents?

sentences.zh: 王子請數月之喪，孟子曰：『雖加一日愈於已。』

translations.literal: The prince asked for mourning of several months; Mencius said, "Though it were one day more, it would be better than none.
translations.idiomatic: When a prince asked for mourning of only a few months, Mencius said, "Even one day more would be better than stopping altogether.

sentences.zh: 聖賢之訓何如也？

translations.literal: What are the teachings of sages and worthies?
translations.idiomatic: What do the sages teach on this?

sentences.zh: 在律，雖編氓小吏，匿喪有禁；

translations.literal: In the law, even commoners and petty clerks are forbidden to conceal mourning;
translations.idiomatic: Under the law, even commoners and petty clerks are forbidden to conceal a death;

sentences.zh: 惟武人得墨缞從事，非所以處輔弼也。

translations.literal: only military men may wear ink mourning and continue in service—not how to treat a chief counselor.
translations.idiomatic: only soldiers may wear ink mourning and remain on duty—that is no way to treat a chief counselor.

sentences.zh: 即雲起復有故事，亦未有一日不出國門，而遽起視事者。

translations.literal: Even if rising from mourning while still in mourning has precedent, never has one not left the state gate for a single day and then abruptly resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: Even if recall from mourning while still in mourning has precedent, never has a man failed to leave the capital for a single day and then abruptly resumed office.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之制何如也？

translations.literal: What are the regulations of the ancestors?
translations.idiomatic: What do the ancestral regulations say?

sentences.zh: 事系萬古綱常，四方視聽，惟今日無過舉，然後後世無遺議。

translations.literal: The matter concerns eternal constants of morality and the eyes and ears of the four quarters; only if today there is no wrongful act will later ages have no lingering censure.
translations.idiomatic: This touches the moral order for all time and the eyes of the realm; only if Your Majesty commits no error today will posterity have no reproach to leave behind.

sentences.zh: 銷變之道，無逾此者。」

translations.literal: The way to dispel this omen—none surpasses this."
translations.idiomatic: There is no better way to dispel this portent than this."

sentences.zh: 疏既上，以副封白居正。

translations.literal: After the memorial had been submitted, he showed the duplicate sealed copy to Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: After submitting the memorial, he showed the sealed copy to Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 居正愕然曰：「疏進耶？」

translations.literal: Juzheng said in astonishment, "Has the memorial been entered?
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng said in astonishment, "Has the memorial gone in?

sentences.zh: 中行曰：「未進不敢白也。」

translations.literal: Zhongxing said, "Not yet entered—I dared not inform you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing said, "Not yet—I dared not tell you before it went in."

sentences.zh: 明日，趙用賢疏入。

translations.literal: The next day Zhao Yongxian's memorial entered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhao Yongxian's memorial was submitted.

sentences.zh: 又明日，艾穆、沈思孝疏入。

translations.literal: The day after, the memorials of Ai Mu and Shen Sixiao entered.
translations.idiomatic: The day after that came memorials from Ai Mu and Shen Sixiao.

sentences.zh: 居正怒，謀於馮保，欲廷杖之。

translations.literal: Juzheng was angry, consulted with Feng Bao, and wished to beat them at court.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng was furious; he consulted Feng Bao and wanted them beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 翰林院侍講趙誌臯、張位、於慎行、張一桂、田一俊、李長春，修撰習孔教、沈懋學俱具疏救，格不入。

translations.literal: Hanlin lecturers Zhao Zhigao, Zhang Wei, Yu Shenxing, Zhang Yigui, Tian Yijun, and Li Changchun, and compilers Xi Kongjiao and Shen Maoxue all submitted memorials to save them; all were blocked and not entered.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin lecturers Zhao Zhigao, Zhang Wei, Yu Shenxing, Zhang Yigui, Tian Yijun, and Li Changchun, and compilers Xi Kongjiao and Shen Maoxue all submitted memorials in their defense; none was accepted.
