sentences.zh: 學士王錫爵乃會詞臣數十人，求解於居正，弗納。

translations.literal: Academician Wang Xijue then gathered several dozen literary officials to beg Juzheng for leniency; he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Wang Xijue then gathered several dozen literary officials to plead with Juzheng for mercy; he refused.

sentences.zh: 遂杖中行等四人。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhongxing and the other four were beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing and the other four were then beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 明日，進士鄒元標疏爭，亦廷杖，五人者，直聲震天下。

translations.literal: The next day jinshi Zou Yuanbiao memorialized in protest and was also beaten at court; the five men's upright reputation shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the jinshi Zou Yuanbiao protested in a memorial and was beaten at court as well; the five men's reputation for integrity resounded throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 中行、用賢並稱吳、趙。

translations.literal: Zhongxing and Yongxian were together called Wu and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing and Yongxian came to be known together as Wu and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 南京御史朱鴻謨疏救五人，亦被斥。

translations.literal: Nanjing censor Zhu Hongmo memorialized to save the five and was also dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing censor Zhu Hongmo memorialized in their defense and was dismissed as well.

sentences.zh: 中行等受杖畢，校尉以布曳出長安門，舁以板扉，即日驅出都城。

translations.literal: When Zhongxing and the others had been beaten, guards dragged them out Chang'an Gate in cloth, carried them on plank doors, and the same day drove them from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After the beating, guards dragged Zhongxing and the others out Chang'an Gate wrapped in cloth, carried them on plank doors, and expelled them from the capital that same day.

sentences.zh: 中行氣息已絕，中書舍人秦柱挾醫至，投藥一匕，乃蘇。

translations.literal: Zhongxing's breath had already ceased; Secretariat drafter Qin Zhu brought a physician, gave one spoonful of medicine, and he revived.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing had stopped breathing; Secretariat drafter Qin Zhu brought a physician, gave him a spoonful of medicine, and he came back to life.

sentences.zh: 輿疾南歸，刲去腐肉數十臠，大者盈掌，深至寸，一肢遂空。

translations.literal: He was carried south ill; dozens of pieces of rotten flesh were cut away, large ones filling the palm, an inch deep; one limb was left hollow.
translations.idiomatic: He was carried home to the south, grievously wounded; dozens of pieces of rotten flesh were cut away, some as large as a palm and an inch deep, until one limb was hollowed out.

sentences.zh: 九年，大計京官，列五人察籍，錮不復敘。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, at the general evaluation of capital officials, the five were listed on the scrutiny register and barred from further appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, at the general evaluation of capital officials, the five were entered on the scrutiny register and permanently barred from office.

sentences.zh: 居正死，士楚當按蘇、松，憮然曰：「吾何面目見吳、趙二公！」

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, Shichu was to inspect Suzhou and Songjiang and said in dejection, "With what face can I meet the two lords Wu and Zhao!
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death, Shichu was assigned to inspect Suzhou and Songjiang and said in anguish, "How can I face Lords Wu and Zhao!

sentences.zh: 遂引疾去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he pleaded illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and resigned.

sentences.zh: 三謨已擢太常少卿，尋與士楚俱被劾削籍。

translations.literal: Sanmo had already been promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; soon he and Shichu were both impeached and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Sanmo had already been promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; soon he and Shichu were both impeached and struck from the register.

sentences.zh: 廷臣交薦中行，召復故官，進右中允，直經筵。

translations.literal: Court officials repeatedly recommended Zhongxing; he was recalled to his former office, promoted to right lecturing attendant, and served at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials repeatedly recommended Zhongxing; he was recalled to his former post, promoted to right lecturing attendant, and served at the Classics Colloquium.

sentences.zh: 大學士許國攻李植、江東之，詆中行、用賢為其黨。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Xu Guo attacked Li Zhi and Jiang Dongzhi, denouncing Zhongxing and Yongxian as their faction.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Xu Guo attacked Li Zhi and Jiang Dongzhi and denounced Zhongxing and Yongxian as members of their clique.

sentences.zh: 中行奏辨，因乞罷，不許。

translations.literal: Zhongxing memorialized in defense and asked to resign; not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing memorialized in his own defense and asked to resign; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 再遷右諭德。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to right preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to right preceptor.

sentences.zh: 御史蔡系周劾植，復侵中行，中行求去，章四上。

translations.literal: Censor Cai Xizhou impeached Zhi and again implicated Zhongxing; Zhongxing sought to leave; four memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Cai Xizhou impeached Zhi and again dragged Zhongxing into the matter; Zhongxing asked to resign and submitted four memorials.

sentences.zh: 詔賜白金、文綺，馳傳歸。

translations.literal: An edict granted him white silver and patterned silk and sent him home by dispatch relay.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him silver and brocade and sent him home by imperial relay.

sentences.zh: 言者屢薦，執政抑不召。

translations.literal: Critics repeatedly recommended him; the chief ministers suppressed and did not summon him.
translations.idiomatic: Critics repeatedly recommended him, but those in power blocked his recall.

sentences.zh: 久之，起侍講學士，掌南京翰林院。

translations.literal: After a long time he was raised as lecturing academician and directed the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed lecturing academician and put in charge of the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 同里僉事徐常吉嘗訟中行，事已解，給事中王嘉謨復摭舊事劾之，命家居俟召。

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Vice Commissioner Xu Changji had once sued Zhongxing; the matter had been resolved; supervising secretary Wang Jiamo again dredged up old affairs to impeach him; he was ordered to remain at home awaiting summons.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow townsman Vice Commissioner Xu Changji had once brought suit against him; that matter had been settled; supervising secretary Wang Jiamo then dredged up old charges to impeach him again, and he was ordered to remain at home awaiting recall.

sentences.zh: 尋卒。

translations.literal: Soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 後贈禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was later posthumously made Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子亮、元，從子宗達。

translations.literal: His sons Liang and Yuan, and his nephew Zongda.
translations.idiomatic: He had sons Liang and Yuan, and a nephew Zongda.

sentences.zh: 亮官御史，坐累貶官，終大理少禦。

translations.literal: Liang served as censor, was demoted on account of implication in a case, and ended as Vice Director of the Grand Court.
translations.idiomatic: Liang served as a censor, was demoted when implicated in a case, and ended his career as Vice Director of the Grand Court.

sentences.zh: 元，江西布政使。

translations.literal: Yuan was administrative commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan became administrative commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 宗達，少傅、建極殿大學士。

translations.literal: Zongda was Junior Tutor and Grand Secretary of the Jianji Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zongda rose to Junior Tutor and Grand Secretary of the Jianji Hall.

sentences.zh: 亮尚誌節，與顧憲成諸人善。

translations.literal: Liang still valued integrity and was on good terms with Gu Xiancheng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Liang still prized integrity and was close to Gu Xiancheng and his circle.

sentences.zh: 而元深疾東林，所輯《吾徵錄》，詆毀不遺力。

translations.literal: Yuan deeply hated the Eastern Forest faction; in his compiled Records of My Travels he slandered them without sparing effort.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, by contrast, loathed the Eastern Forest faction and in his compiled Records of My Travels attacked them relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 兄弟異趣如此。

translations.literal: The brothers' divergent inclinations were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Between the brothers the contrast was that sharp.

sentences.zh: 趙用賢，字汝師，常熟人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yongxian, styled Rushi, was a man of Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yongxian, styled Rushi, was a native of Changshu.

sentences.zh: 父承謙，廣東參議。

translations.literal: His father Chengqian was a participant in the administration of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengqian served as administrative vice commissioner of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 用賢舉隆慶五年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: Yongxian passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Longqing and was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Longqing Yongxian passed the jinshi examination and was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，授檢討。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 張居正父喪奪情，用賢抗疏曰：「臣竊怪居正能以君臣之義效忠於數年，不能以父子之情少盡於一日。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng's father died and he was released from mourning to continue in office, Yongxian submitted a defiant memorial, saying: "Your servant privately marvels that Juzheng could devote himself in the righteousness of ruler and minister for several years, yet could not fulfill the feeling of father and son even for one day.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng's father died and he was released from mourning to remain in office, Yongxian submitted a defiant memorial: "I find it strange that Juzheng could serve loyally as minister for years in the name of duty between ruler and subject, yet could not honor for a single day the bond between father and son.

sentences.zh: 臣又竊怪居正之勛望積以數年，而陛下忽敗之一旦。

translations.literal: Your servant again privately marvels that Juzheng's merit and prestige accumulated over several years, yet Your Majesty suddenly ruined them in a single morning.
translations.idiomatic: I am also struck that Juzheng's merit and standing had been built up over years, only for Your Majesty to undo it all in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 莫若如先朝楊溥、李賢故事，聽其暫還守制，刻期赴闕，庶父子音容乖暌阻絕於十有九年者，得區區稍伸其痛於臨穴憑棺之一慟也。

translations.literal: Better to follow the precedent of the previous dynasty's Yang Pu and Li Xian: allow him to return temporarily to observe mourning, fix a date to come to court, so that father and son, whose voices and faces have been estranged and cut off for nineteen years, may in some small measure release their grief in the one lamentation of standing at the grave and leaning on the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Better to follow the Yang Pu and Li Xian precedents of the previous reign: let him go home briefly to complete mourning, with a fixed date to return to court, so that a father and son kept apart in life for nineteen years may at least pour out some fraction of their grief at the grave.

sentences.zh: 國家設臺諫以司法紀、任糾繩，乃今嘵嘵為輔臣請留，背公議而徇私情，蔑至性而創異論。

translations.literal: The state established the censorate and remonstrance offices to uphold the law and discipline and to bear the charge of correction, yet now they clamor to keep the chief minister, turning their backs on public opinion to indulge private feeling, scorning utmost filial nature to invent heterodox doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: The state created the censorate and remonstrance bureaus to uphold law and discipline and to hold officials to account—yet now they clamor to keep the chief minister in office, siding with private feeling against public opinion and scorning the deepest obligations of filial piety to invent a new doctrine.

sentences.zh: 臣愚竊懼士氣之日靡，國是之日淆也。」

translations.literal: Your servant, foolish, privately fears that scholar-official spirit daily declines and that the settled policy of the state daily grows confused."
translations.idiomatic: I fear in my folly that the moral fiber of the scholar-official class is being worn down day by day, and that the settled direction of the state is being muddied."

sentences.zh: 疏入，與中行同杖除名。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, he was beaten with the rod and removed from office, the same as Zhongxing.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was received, he was beaten and dismissed from office, as Wu Zhongxing had been.

sentences.zh: 用賢體素肥，肉潰落如掌，其妻臘而藏之。

translations.literal: Yongxian's body had always been stout; flesh putrefied and fell away in pieces the size of a palm, and his wife preserved it in wax and stored it.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxian had always been heavyset; after the beating, flesh sloughed off in palm-sized pieces, and his wife preserved it in wax and kept it.

sentences.zh: 用賢有女許御史吳之彥子鎮。

translations.literal: Yongxian had a daughter betrothed to the son Zhen of the censor Wu Zhiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxian had a daughter betrothed to Zhen, son of the censor Wu Zhiyan.

sentences.zh: 之彥懼及，深結居正，得巡撫福建。

translations.literal: Zhiyan feared implication; he formed a deep tie with Juzheng and obtained appointment as grand coordinator of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would be implicated, Zhiyan cultivated a close alliance with Juzheng and secured appointment as grand coordinator of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 過裏門，不為用賢禮，且坐鎮於其弟下，曰：「婢子也」，以激用賢。

translations.literal: Passing through the native gate, he did not pay Yongxian the proper courtesy, and moreover seated Zhen below his younger brother, saying, "A servant girl," to provoke Yongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through his home district, he refused to pay Yongxian the proper courtesy and seated Zhen below his own younger brother, saying, "She is but a servant girl," to goad Yongxian.

sentences.zh: 用賢怒，已察知其受居正黨王篆指，遂反幣告絕。

translations.literal: Yongxian was enraged; he had already perceived that Zhiyan acted at the direction of Juzheng's partisan Wang Zhuan, and so returned the betrothal gifts and announced the engagement broken.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxian, enraged, had already seen that Zhiyan was acting at the instigation of Juzheng's partisan Wang Zhuan; he returned the betrothal gifts and broke off the match.

sentences.zh: 之彥大喜。

translations.literal: Zhiyan was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyan was delighted.

sentences.zh: 居正死之明年，用賢復故官，進右贊善。

translations.literal: In the year after Juzheng died, Yongxian was restored to his former office and promoted to Right Supplementer.
translations.idiomatic: The year after Juzheng died, Yongxian was restored to office and promoted to Right Supplementer.

sentences.zh: 江東之、李植輩爭向之，物望皆屬焉。

translations.literal: Jiang Dongzhi, Li Zhi, and their like competed to court him, and public esteem all turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Dongzhi, Li Zhi, and their circle vied to align with him, and public esteem settled on him.

sentences.zh: 而用賢性剛，負氣傲物，數訾議大臣得失，申時行、許國等忌之。

translations.literal: But Yongxian's nature was rigid; he bore himself with proud spirit and looked down on others, repeatedly criticizing the merits and faults of great ministers, and Shen Shixing, Xu Guo, and others resented him.
translations.idiomatic: But Yongxian was stiff by nature, proud and quick to look down on others; he repeatedly passed judgment on the great ministers' conduct, and Shen Shixing, Xu Guo, and others came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 會植、東之攻時行，國遂力詆植、東之，而陰斥用賢、中行，謂：「昔之專恣在權貴，今乃在下僚；

translations.literal: When Zhi and Dongzhi attacked Shixing, Guo then vigorously denounced Zhi and Dongzhi, while covertly censuring Yongxian and Zhongxing, saying: "Formerly arbitrariness lay with powerful nobles; now it lies with lower officials;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zhi and Jiang Dongzhi attacked Shen Shixing, Xu Guo vigorously denounced them while covertly censuring Yongxian and Wu Zhongxing, saying: "In the past, willful power lay with the mighty at court; now it lies with junior officials;

sentences.zh: 昔顛倒是非在小人，今乃在君子。

translations.literal: Formerly inverting right and wrong lay with petty men; now it lies with gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, twisting right and wrong was the work of petty men; now it is the work of gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 意氣感激，偶成一二事，遂自負不世之節，號召浮薄喜事之人，黨同伐異，罔上行私，其風不可長。」

translations.literal: Stirred by righteous indignation, they chance to accomplish one or two things, then pride themselves on peerless integrity, summon frivolous men who delight in trouble, band together to attack the unlike, deceive their superiors for private ends—such a wind cannot be allowed to grow."
translations.idiomatic: Stirred by righteous indignation, they chance upon one or two successes and fancy themselves men of unrivaled integrity; they rally the frivolous and meddlesome, band together to attack their foes, and deceive their superiors for private ends. Such a spirit cannot be indulged."

sentences.zh: 於是用賢抗辨求去，極言朋黨之說，小人以之去君子、空人國，詞甚激憤。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yongxian argued defiantly and requested leave, speaking at length on the doctrine of factions—that petty men use it to remove gentlemen and empty the state of men—his words very indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxian answered in a defiant memorial asking to resign, arguing at length that the charge of faction is a tool by which petty men drive out gentlemen and leave the state without worthy men; his language was fiercely indignant.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽其去。

translations.literal: The emperor did not approve his resignation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to let him go.

sentences.zh: 黨論之興，遂自此始。

translations.literal: The rise of factional discourse thus began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of factional politics dates from this moment.

sentences.zh: 尋充經筵講官。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed lecturer at the Classics Mat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed lecturer at the imperial lecture series.

sentences.zh: 再遷右庶子，改南京祭酒。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Right Sublector and transferred to be libationer at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Right Sublector, then transferred to serve as libationer at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 薦舉人王之士、鄧元錫、劉元卿，清修積學。

translations.literal: He recommended the licentiates Wang Zhishi, Deng Yuanxi, and Liu Yuanqing, men of pure conduct and accumulated learning.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended the licentiates Wang Zhishi, Deng Yuanxi, and Liu Yuanqing—scholars of pure conduct and deep learning.

sentences.zh: 又請建儲，宥言官李沂罪。

translations.literal: He also requested that the heir be established and that the crime of the remonstrating official Li Yi be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that a crown prince be named and that the remonstrating official Li Yi be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 居三年，擢南京禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: After three years in office, he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Right in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 以吏部郎中趙南星薦，改北部。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Zhao Nanxing, director in the Ministry of Personnel, he was transferred to the northern capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the recommendation of Zhao Nanxing, a director in the Ministry of Personnel, he was transferred to the northern capital.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼教習庶吉士。

translations.literal: Soon, with his present rank, he was concurrently made instructor of Hanlin bachelors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was given his present rank while also serving as instructor to the Hanlin bachelors.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，王錫爵復入內閣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Wang Xijue again entered the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of the reign, Wang Xijue returned to the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 初，用賢徙南，中行、思孝、植、東之已前貶，或罷去，故執政安之。

translations.literal: At first, when Yongxian was moved south, Zhongxing, Sixiao, Zhi, and Dongzhi had already been demoted earlier or dismissed, and so the administration was at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yongxian had been sent south, Wu Zhongxing, Shen Sixiao, Li Zhi, and Jiang Dongzhi had already been demoted or dismissed, and the ruling ministers had felt secure.

sentences.zh: 及是，用賢復以爭三王並封語侵錫爵，為所銜。

translations.literal: Now Yongxian again offended Xijue with words opposing the concurrent enfeoffment of the three princes, and Xijue bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yongxian again gave offense with his opposition to the concurrent enfeoffment of the three princes, and Xijue nursed a grievance against him.

sentences.zh: 會改吏部左侍郎，與文選郎顧憲成辨論人才，群情益附，錫爵不便也。

translations.literal: When he was changed to Left Vice Minister of Personnel and debated talent with Gu Xiancheng, the Selection Secretary, public sentiment increasingly attached to him, and Xijue was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When he was appointed Left Vice Minister of Personnel and debated the merits of officials with Gu Xiancheng, the Selection Secretary, public sentiment rallied to him all the more, to Xijue's discomfort.

sentences.zh: 用賢故所絕婚吳之彥者，錫爵裏人，時以僉事論罷，使其子鎮訐用賢論財逐婿，蔑法棄倫。

translations.literal: Wu Zhiyan, whom Yongxian had formerly broken off in betrothal, was a fellow townsman of Xijue; at the time he had been dismissed from office as vice commissioner on charges, and he had his son Zhen accuse Yongxian of using money to drive out a son-in-law, scorning the law and abandoning propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhiyan, whose betrothal Yongxian had broken off, was a fellow townsman of Xijue's; recently dismissed as a vice commissioner on charges, he had his son Zhen accuse Yongxian of using money to drive out a son-in-law—an attack that scorned law and abandoned moral order.

sentences.zh: 用賢疏辨，乞休。

translations.literal: Yongxian submitted a memorial in defense and requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxian submitted a memorial in his own defense and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 詔禮官平議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Rites officials to adjudicate fairly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Ministry of Rites to adjudicate the matter fairly.

sentences.zh: 尚書羅萬化以之彥其門生，引嫌力辭。

translations.literal: The minister Luo Wanhua, because Zhiyan was his student, cited conflict of interest and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The minister Luo Wanhua, citing conflict of interest because Zhiyan was his student, firmly declined to sit in judgment.

sentences.zh: 錫爵乃上議曰：「用賢輕絕，之彥緩發，均失也。

translations.literal: Xijue then submitted an opinion, saying: "Yongxian rashly broke the engagement; Zhiyan was slow to lodge his accusation—both were at fault.
translations.idiomatic: Xijue then submitted his opinion: "Yongxian broke the engagement too lightly, and Zhiyan was slow to bring his accusation—both were in the wrong.

sentences.zh: 今趙女已嫁，難問初盟；

translations.literal: Now Zhao's daughter is already married; it is hard to question the original betrothal;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao's daughter is already married elsewhere, so the original betrothal cannot be revisited;

sentences.zh: 吳男未婚，無容反坐。

translations.literal: Wu Zhiyan's son is unmarried; there is no ground for reverse conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhiyan's son remains unmarried, so there is no basis to convict him in turn.

sentences.zh: 欲折其衷，宜聽用賢引疾，而曲貸之彥。」

translations.literal: To split the difference, Yongxian should be allowed to cite illness and retire, while Zhiyan should be leniently excused."
translations.idiomatic: To strike a balance, Yongxian should be allowed to retire on grounds of illness, while Zhiyan should be leniently excused."

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved his recommendation.

sentences.zh: 用賢遂免歸。

translations.literal: Yongxian was then dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxian was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 戶部郎中楊應宿、鄭材復力詆用賢，請據律行法。

translations.literal: Yang Yingsu and Zheng Cai, directors in the Ministry of Revenue, again vigorously denounced Yongxian and requested that the law be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yingsu and Zheng Cai, directors in the Ministry of Revenue, again attacked Yongxian vigorously and demanded that he be punished under the law.

sentences.zh: 都御史李世達、侍郎李禎疏直用賢，斥兩人讒諂，遂為所攻。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief Li Shida and the vice minister Li Zhen submitted memorials supporting Yongxian and denouncing the two men's slander and flattery; they were then attacked by them.
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief Li Shida and Vice Minister Li Zhen submitted memorials in Yongxian's defense, denouncing the two men as slanderers and flatterers; they in turn came under attack.

sentences.zh: 高攀龍、吳弘濟、譚一召、孫繼有、安希範輩皆坐論救褫職。

translations.literal: Gao Panlong, Wu Hongji, Tan Yizhao, Sun Jiyou, An Xifan, and their like were all punished for pleading in his defense and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Panlong, Wu Hongji, Tan Yizhao, Sun Jiyou, An Xifan, and others were all punished for speaking up on his behalf and stripped of their posts.

sentences.zh: 自是朋黨論益熾。

translations.literal: From this the discourse of factions grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: From this point factional politics burned hotter still.

sentences.zh: 中行、用賢、植、東之創於前，元標、南星、憲成、攀龍繼之。

translations.literal: Zhongxing, Yongxian, Zhi, and Dongzhi initiated it earlier; Yuanbiao, Nanxing, Xiancheng, and Panlong followed.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, Li Zhi, and Jiang Dongzhi had opened the way; Zou Yuanbiao, Zhao Nanxing, Gu Xiancheng, and Gao Panlong carried it on.

sentences.zh: 言事者益裁量執政，執政日與枝拄，水火薄射，訖於明亡雲。

translations.literal: Those who spoke on affairs increasingly weighed and judged the administration; the administration daily clashed with them—fire and water, arrows flying close—and so it continued until the fall of the Ming, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators increasingly sat in judgment over the ministers in power, and those ministers clashed with them day after day like fire against water, arrows flying close—until, it is said, the dynasty fell.

sentences.zh: 用賢長身聳肩，議論風發，有經濟大略。

translations.literal: Yongxian was tall in stature with raised shoulders; in debate his words burst forth like wind, and he possessed a broad vision for statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxian was tall and broad-shouldered; his speech came in gusts, and he had a statesman's grasp of practical policy.

sentences.zh: 蘇、松、嘉、湖諸府，財賦敵天下半，民生坐困。

translations.literal: In the prefectures of Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou, fiscal revenue rivaled half the empire, and the people's livelihood sat trapped in hardship.
translations.idiomatic: In Suzhou, Songjiang, Jiaxing, and Huzhou, tax revenue rivaled half the empire, while the common people languished under the burden.

sentences.zh: 用賢官庶子時，與進士袁黃商榷數十晝夜，條十四事上之。

translations.literal: When Yongxian served as sublector, he and the jinshi Yuan Huang discussed for dozens of days and nights and set forth fourteen items in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as sublector, he and the jinshi Yuan Huang debated for many days and nights and submitted a memorial listing fourteen reforms.

sentences.zh: 時行、錫爵以為吳人不當言吳事，調旨切責，寢不行。

translations.literal: Shixing and Xijue held that men of Wu should not speak on Wu affairs; an edict sharply rebuked him, and the proposal was shelved and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing and Wang Xijue held that a man of Wu had no business speaking on Wu affairs; the court issued a sharp rebuke, and the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 家居四年卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home four years and then died.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in retirement for four years and then died.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，贈太子少保、禮部尚書，謚文毅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was posthumously endowed as Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince and Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 孫士春、士錦，崇禎十年同舉進士。

translations.literal: His grandsons Shichun and Shijin both passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons Shichun and Shijin both passed the jinshi examination in the tenth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 士春，字景之。

translations.literal: Shichun, styled Jingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shichun, styled Jingzhi.

sentences.zh: 第三人及第，授編修。

translations.literal: He placed third in the examination and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He placed third in the palace examination and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 明年，兵部尚書楊嗣昌奪情視事，未幾入閣。

translations.literal: The next year, Yang Sichang, Minister of War, was released from mourning to conduct affairs; before long he entered the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Yang Sichang, Minister of War, was released from mourning to resume office and soon entered the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 少詹事黃道周劾之，下獄。

translations.literal: The Junior Mentor Huang Daozhou impeached him, and he was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Junior Mentor Huang Daozhou impeached him, and he was thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 士春上疏曰：「嗣昌墨衰視事，既已罔效，陛下簡入綸扉，自應力辭新命。

translations.literal: Shichun submitted a memorial, saying: "Sichang, in ink mourning, conducts affairs; he has already proved ineffective. Your Majesty has singled him out for the silk gate; he ought firmly to decline the new appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Shichun submitted a memorial: "Sichang has been conducting affairs while still in mourning dress, and he has already proved ineffective. Your Majesty has summoned him to the Grand Secretariat; he ought firmly to decline the new appointment.

sentences.zh: 乃閱其奏牘，徒計歲月久近間，絕無哀痛惻怛之念，何奸悖一至此也！

translations.literal: Yet on reading his memorials, one finds only calculation of how near or far the months are, utterly no thought of grief or tender compassion—how wicked and perverse can it be to this degree!
translations.idiomatic: Yet reading his memorials, one finds only calculations of how many months have passed—no trace of grief or compassion. How wicked and perverse can a man become!

sentences.zh: 陛下破格奪情，曰人才不足故耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty exceptionally released him from mourning, saying it was because talent was insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty made an exceptional release from mourning, saying there were not enough men of talent.

sentences.zh: 不知人才所以不振，正由愛功名、薄忠孝致之。

translations.literal: You do not know that the reason talent fails to flourish is precisely that men cherish fame and slight loyalty and filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: You do not see that talent fails to flourish precisely because men prize fame and slight loyalty and filial piety.

sentences.zh: 且無事不講儲材，有事輕言破格，非用人無弊之道也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in times without trouble one always speaks of stockpiling talent, yet in times of trouble one lightly speaks of exceptions—this is not the flawless way of employing men.
translations.idiomatic: In peace you speak constantly of nurturing talent, yet in crisis you lightly invoke exceptions to the rules—this is not a sound way to employ men.

sentences.zh: 臣祖用賢，首論故相奪情，幾斃杖下，臘敗肉示子孫。

translations.literal: Your servant's grandfather Yongxian was the first to argue against the former chief minister's release from mourning; he nearly died under the rod, and preserved the putrefied flesh in wax to show his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: My grandfather Yongxian was the first to protest when the former chief minister was released from mourning; he nearly died under the rod, and preserved the flesh that had sloughed from his wounds in wax to show his descendants.

sentences.zh: 臣敢背家學，負明主，坐視綱常掃地哉？」

translations.literal: Dare your servant betray his family's teaching, fail his enlightened lord, and sit watching while the pillars of propriety are swept to the ground?"
translations.idiomatic: How could I betray my family's teaching, fail my enlightened sovereign, and sit by while the pillars of moral order are swept away?"

sentences.zh: 帝怒，謫廣東布政司照磨。

translations.literal: The emperor was enraged and demoted him to registrar in the Guangdong administrative commission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and demoted him to registrar in the Guangdong administrative commission.

sentences.zh: 祖孫並以攻執政奪情斥，士論重之。

translations.literal: Grandfather and grandson were both expelled for attacking the administration over the release from mourning, and scholarly opinion esteemed them.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather and grandson were both cast out for attacking the ministers over the release from mourning, and men of learning held them in high regard.

sentences.zh: 後復故官，終左中允。

translations.literal: Later he was restored to his former office and ended as Left Household Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored to office and ended his career as Left Household Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 艾穆，字和父，平江人。

translations.literal: Ai Mu, styled Hefu, was a man of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Mu, styled Hefu, was a native of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 以鄉舉署阜城教諭，鄰郡諸生趙南星、喬璧星皆就學焉。

translations.literal: Through the provincial examination he was appointed acting instructor at Fucheng; the students Zhao Nanxing and Qiao Bixing from a neighboring prefecture all came to study under him.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the provincial examination, he was appointed acting instructor at Fucheng; Zhao Nanxing and Qiao Bixing, students from a neighboring prefecture, both studied under him.

sentences.zh: 入為國子助教。

translations.literal: He entered service as assistant instructor at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an assistant instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 張居正知穆名，欲用為誥敕房中書舍人，不應。

translations.literal: Zhang Juzheng knew Mu's reputation and wished to employ him as a drafting secretary in the Edict Bureau; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Juzheng knew Mu by reputation and wished to appoint him as a drafting secretary in the Edict Bureau, but Mu declined.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，擢刑部主事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 進員外郎，錄囚陜西。

translations.literal: He advanced to vice director and reviewed prisoners in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director and sent to review prisoners in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 時居正法嚴，決囚不如額者罪。

translations.literal: At the time Juzheng's law was strict: failure to execute prisoners up to the quota was a crime.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Juzheng's law was strict—officials who failed to execute prisoners up to the quota were themselves punished.

sentences.zh: 穆與御史議，止決二人。

translations.literal: Mu deliberated with the censor and only ordered the execution of two men.
translations.idiomatic: Mu discussed the matter with the censor and authorized the execution of only two men.

sentences.zh: 御史懼不稱，穆曰：「我終不以人命博官也。」

translations.literal: The censor feared not meeting the quota; Mu said, "I will never trade men's lives for office."
translations.idiomatic: The censor feared they would not meet the quota; Mu said, "I will never trade men's lives for promotion."

sentences.zh: 還朝，居正盛氣譙讓。

translations.literal: On returning to court, Juzheng in full wrath reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to court, Juzheng confronted him in a towering rage.

sentences.zh: 穆曰：「主上沖年，小臣體好生德，佐公平允之治，有罪甘之。」

translations.literal: Mu said, "The lord is in his tender years; this minor official embodies the virtue of sparing life and assists in fair and balanced governance—if there is guilt, I accept it gladly."
translations.idiomatic: Mu said, "The sovereign is still young; as a minor official I embody the virtue of sparing life and assist in fair and balanced governance—if I am guilty, I accept punishment willingly."

sentences.zh: 揖而退。

translations.literal: He bowed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 及居正遭喪奪情，穆私居嘆息，遂與主事沈思孝抗疏諫曰：「自居正奪情，妖星突見，光逼中天。

translations.literal: When Juzheng met bereavement and was released from mourning to remain in office, Mu sighed in private at home, then joined the director Shen Sixiao in submitting a defiant memorial of remonstrance, saying: "Since Juzheng's release from mourning, an evil star has suddenly appeared, its light pressing upon the zenith.
translations.idiomatic: When Juzheng's father died and he was released from mourning to remain in office, Mu sighed at home, then joined the director Shen Sixiao in a defiant memorial of remonstrance: "Since Juzheng was released from mourning, an evil star has suddenly appeared, its light pressing upon the zenith.

sentences.zh: 言官曾士楚、陳三謨甘犯清議，率先請留，人心頓死，舉國如狂。

translations.literal: The remonstrating officials Zeng Shichu and Chen Sanmo willingly violated pure opinion and were first to request that he stay; popular sentiment instantly died, and the whole state was like mad.
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrating officials Zeng Shichu and Chen Sanmo willingly defied upright opinion and were first to urge that he stay; public morale collapsed at once, and the whole realm seemed unhinged.

sentences.zh: 今星變未銷，火災繼起。

translations.literal: Now the stellar anomaly has not faded, and fires rise one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The stellar omen has not yet faded, and fires break out one after another.

sentences.zh: 臣敢自愛其死，不灑血一為陛下言之！

translations.literal: How could your servant spare his life and fail to shed his blood once to speak for Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: How could I value my life so highly as to hold back from pouring out my heart's blood once for Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 陛下之留居正也，動曰為社稷故。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's keeping of Juzheng always says it is for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: In keeping Juzheng at court, Your Majesty always says it is for the sake of the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 夫社稷所重，莫如綱常。

translations.literal: Of what the altars of state value most, nothing surpasses the pillars of propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Of all that the altars of state depend upon, nothing matters more than the pillars of moral order.

sentences.zh: 而元輔大臣者，綱常之表也。

translations.literal: And the chief minister is the outward model of those pillars.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister is the outward face of those pillars.

sentences.zh: 綱常不顧，何社稷之能安？

translations.literal: If the pillars are not heeded, how can the altars be secure?
translations.idiomatic: If those pillars are ignored, how can the altars of state stand secure?

sentences.zh: 且事偶一為之者，例也；

translations.literal: Moreover, things done once as an exception are precedent;
translations.idiomatic: What is done once as an exception becomes precedent;

sentences.zh: 而萬世不易者，先王之制也。

translations.literal: what never changes for ten thousand generations is the institution of the former kings.
translations.idiomatic: what never changes for ten thousand generations is the institution of the former kings.

sentences.zh: 今棄先王之制，而從近代之例，如之何其可也。

translations.literal: Now to abandon the institutions of the former kings and follow recent precedents—how can this be?
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the institutions of the former kings and follow recent precedents—how can this be permitted?

sentences.zh: 居正今以例留，腆顏就列矣。

translations.literal: Juzheng now stays by precedent and shamelessly takes his seat in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng now remains by precedent and takes his seat in court without shame.

sentences.zh: 異時國家有大慶賀、大祭祀，為元輔者，欲避則害君臣之義，欲出則傷父子之情。

translations.literal: In future, when the state has great celebrations or great sacrifices, as chief minister—if he wishes to avoid them, he harms the duty between ruler and minister; if he wishes to attend, he wounds the feeling between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: When the state holds great celebrations or great sacrifices, the chief minister will be caught either way: to stay away harms the duty between ruler and minister, yet to attend wounds the bond between father and son.

sentences.zh: 臣不知陛下何以處居正，居正又何以自處也！

translations.literal: Your servant does not know how Your Majesty will handle Juzheng, nor how Juzheng will handle himself!
translations.idiomatic: I do not know how Your Majesty will resolve this for Juzheng, nor how Juzheng will resolve it for himself!

sentences.zh: 徐庶以母故辭於昭烈曰：『臣方寸亂矣。』

translations.literal: Xu Shu, for his mother's sake, declined before Lord Bei, saying: 'Your servant's heart is in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Shu declined Liu Bei for his mother's sake, he said, "My heart is in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 居正獨非人子而方寸不亂耶？

translations.literal: Is Juzheng alone not a son, yet his heart is not in turmoil?
translations.idiomatic: Is Juzheng not also a son—yet his heart is untroubled?

sentences.zh: 位極人臣，反不修匹夫常節，何以對天下後世！

translations.literal: Standing at the utmost height among ministers, yet he will not observe the constant propriety of an ordinary man—how can he answer to all under heaven and posterity!
translations.idiomatic: Having risen to the highest rank among ministers, he will not observe the ordinary proprieties of a son—how can he answer to the world and to posterity!

sentences.zh: 臣聞古聖帝明王勸人以孝矣，未聞從而奪之也。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that ancient sage emperors and enlightened kings exhorted men to filial piety; he has never heard that they followed by seizing it away.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the sage emperors of antiquity exhorted men to filial piety; I have never heard that they then seized it away.

sentences.zh: 為人臣者，移孝以事君矣，未聞為所奪也。

translations.literal: As a minister, one shifts filial piety to serve one's lord; one has never heard that it is seized away.
translations.idiomatic: A minister shifts filial piety to the service of his lord; I have never heard that it is taken from him.

sentences.zh: 以禮義廉恥風天下猶恐不足，顧乃奪之，使天下為人子者，皆忘三年之愛於其父，常紀墜矣。

translations.literal: Using ritual, righteousness, shame, and disgrace to wind through all under heaven—one still fears it is insufficient—yet now it is seized away, making all sons under heaven forget the three years' love for their fathers; the constant standards have fallen.
translations.idiomatic: You would use ritual, righteousness, shame, and disgrace to shape the realm, and still fear it is not enough—yet now you seize filial piety away, so that sons everywhere forget the three years' love owed their fathers. The enduring standards of conduct have collapsed.

sentences.zh: 異時即欲以法度整齊之，何可得耶！

translations.literal: When another time comes and you then wish to put things in order with laws and standards, how can it be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: If you ever wish later to restore order through law and ritual, how will that be possible!

sentences.zh: 陛下誠眷居正，當愛之以德，使奔喪終制，以全大節；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly cares for Juzheng, you ought to love him with virtue, enabling him to rush home for mourning and complete the full mourning term, thereby preserving his great integrity;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly esteems Juzheng, you should cherish him through virtue—let him go home for mourning and observe the full term of filial duty, so that his supreme integrity remains intact;

sentences.zh: 則綱常植而朝廷正，朝廷正而百官萬民莫不一於正，災變無不可弭矣。」

translations.literal: then the constant norms will be planted and the court will be upright; when the court is upright, the hundred officials and myriad people will all be unified in rectitude, and no calamity or anomaly cannot be quelled."
translations.idiomatic: then the foundations of propriety will stand firm and the court will be set right; when the court is right, officials and common people alike will follow suit, and no disaster or portent will fail to be allayed."

sentences.zh: 時吳中行、趙用賢請令居正奔喪，葬畢還朝，而穆、思孝直請令終制，故居正尤怒。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Zhongxing and Zhao Yongxian asked that Juzheng be ordered to rush home for mourning and return to court after the burial was complete, whereas Mu and Sixiao directly asked that he complete the full mourning term—therefore Juzheng was all the more furious.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wu Zhongxing and Zhao Yongxian urged that Juzheng be sent home for mourning and recalled after the funeral, while Mu and Sixiao insisted he observe the full mourning period to the end—so Juzheng was especially enraged.

sentences.zh: 中行、用賢杖六十，穆、思孝皆八十加梏堣，置之詔獄。

translations.literal: Zhongxing and Yongxian were beaten sixty strokes; Mu and Sixiao each received eighty strokes with the cangue and fetter added, and were placed in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing and Yongxian were flogged sixty blows; Mu and Sixiao each received eighty blows with cangue and shackles, and were consigned to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 越三日，以門扉舁出城，穆遣戍涼州。

translations.literal: After three days they were carried out of the city on door panels; Mu was banished to garrison duty in Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later they were borne out of the city on door panels; Mu was exiled to garrison service in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 創重不省人事，既而復蘇，遂詣戍所。

translations.literal: His wounds were grave and he lost consciousness; after he revived, he proceeded to his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: His injuries were severe and he lost consciousness; once he recovered, he made his way to his place of banishment.

sentences.zh: 穆，居正鄉人也。

translations.literal: Mu was a fellow townsman of Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was from the same home district as Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 居正語人曰：「昔嚴分宜時未有同鄉攻擊者，我不得比分宜矣。」

translations.literal: Juzheng said to others: "In the time of Lord Yan of Fenyi there were none from his home district who attacked him; I cannot compare with Fenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng remarked to others, "In Yan Song's day no one from his own district assailed him—I am not fit to be compared with Fenyi.

sentences.zh: 九年，大計，復置穆、思孝察籍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, at the grand assessment, Mu and Sixiao were again placed on the surveillance register.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, at the triennial evaluation, Mu and Sixiao were again entered on the surveillance rolls.

sentences.zh: 及居正死，言官交薦，起戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, censorial officials recommended him in succession, and he was raised to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death, remonstrating officials recommended him in turn, and he was recalled as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷西川僉事，屢遷太仆少卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Western Sichuan, and after several promotions became Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Vice Commissioner in western Sichuan and, after several promotions, became Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 十九年秋，擢右僉都御史，巡撫四川。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the nineteenth year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and toured as Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the nineteenth year he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and appointed Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 故崇陽知縣周應中、賓州知州葉春及行義過人，穆舉以自代，不報。

translations.literal: The former magistrate of Chongyang Zhou Yingzhong, the prefect of Binzhou Ye Chunji, and others whose conduct and righteousness surpassed ordinary men—Mu recommended them to succeed himself; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The former magistrate of Chongyang, Zhou Yingzhong, the prefect of Binzhou, Ye Chunji, and others of outstanding conduct—Mu recommended them to succeed him, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 既之官，有告播州宣慰使楊應龍叛者，貴州巡撫葉夢熊請征之。

translations.literal: After he took up his post, someone reported that Yang Yinglong, Pacification Commissioner of Bozhou, had rebelled; Ye Mengxiong, Grand Coordinator of Guizhou, asked to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, word came that Yang Yinglong, Pacification Commissioner of Bozhou, had rebelled; Ye Mengxiong, Grand Coordinator of Guizhou, petitioned for a punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 蜀人多言應龍強，未易輕舉，穆亦不欲加兵，與夢熊異。

translations.literal: Many in Shu said Yinglong was strong and not to be taken lightly; Mu also did not wish to add troops, differing from Mengxiong.
translations.idiomatic: Many in Sichuan said Yinglong was formidable and not to be provoked lightly; Mu too was reluctant to commit troops, and disagreed with Mengxiong.

sentences.zh: 朝命兩撫臣會勘，應龍不願赴貴州，乃逮至重慶，對簿論斬，輸贖，放之還。

translations.literal: The court ordered the two grand coordinators to investigate jointly; Yinglong was unwilling to go to Guizhou, so he was arrested and brought to Chongqing, tried with sentence of decapitation, paid a ransom, and was released to return.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered both coordinators to conduct a joint inquiry; Yinglong refused to go to Guizhou, so he was brought to Chongqing, tried with a capital sentence, ransomed himself, and was sent home.

sentences.zh: 穆病歸，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Mu took ill and returned home; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Mu fell ill and retired; he died not long after.

sentences.zh: 後應龍復叛，議者追咎穆，奪其職。

translations.literal: Later when Yinglong rebelled again, critics blamed Mu retrospectively and stripped his posthumous rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Yinglong rebelled again, critics blamed Mu in hindsight and stripped his posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 喬璧星，臨城人。

translations.literal: Qiao Bixing, a native of Lincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Bixing was a native of Lincheng.

sentences.zh: 官右僉都御史，亦巡撫四川。

translations.literal: He held the office of Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and also toured as Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and likewise as Grand Coordinator of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 葉春及，歸善人。

translations.literal: Ye Chunji, a native of Guishan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Chunji was a native of Guishan.

sentences.zh: 由鄉舉授福清教諭。

translations.literal: Through the provincial recommendation he was appointed Instructor of Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended through the provincial examination, he was appointed Instructor at Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 上書陳時政，纚纚三萬言。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial stating the policies of the time, thirty thousand characters in flowing detail.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on current affairs, a flowing discourse of thirty thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 終戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He ended as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose no higher than Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 沈思孝，字純父，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Shen Sixiao, styled Chunfu, a native of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Sixiao, courtesy name Chunfu, was a native of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 舉隆慶二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Longqing.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the second year of the Longqing reign.

sentences.zh: 又三年，謁選。

translations.literal: Three years later he presented himself for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he presented himself for office.

sentences.zh: 高拱署吏部，欲留為屬曹，思孝辭焉，乃授番禺知縣。

translations.literal: Gao Gong was acting at the Ministry of Personnel and wished to retain him as a subordinate clerk; Sixiao declined, and was then appointed magistrate of Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Gong was acting head of the Ministry of Personnel and wished to keep him on staff; Sixiao declined, and was appointed magistrate of Panyu.

sentences.zh: 殷正茂總制兩廣，欲聽民與番人互市，且開海口諸山征其稅，思孝持不可。

translations.literal: Yin Zhengmao was supreme commander of the two Guang provinces and wished to allow the people to trade with the barbarians and to open Haikou and various mountains to levy taxes; Sixiao held that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhengmao, supreme commander of the two Guang provinces, wished to permit trade between the populace and the tribes, and to open Haikou and the hill country to taxation; Sixiao firmly opposed it.

sentences.zh: 萬歷初，舉卓異，又為刑部主事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wanli he was cited for outstanding merit and again served as a Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wanli reign he was cited for exceptional service and returned to the Ministry of Punishments as a principal secretary.

sentences.zh: 張居正父喪奪情，與艾穆合疏諫。

translations.literal: When Zhang Juzheng's father's death led to retention of office despite mourning, he joined Ai Mu in a joint memorial of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Juzheng was recalled to office despite mourning his father, he joined Ai Mu in a joint memorial of protest.

sentences.zh: 廷杖，戍神電衛。

translations.literal: He was beaten at court and banished to garrison at the Shen Dian Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was flogged at court and exiled to the Shen Dian Guard.

sentences.zh: 居正死，召復官，進光祿少卿。

translations.literal: When Juzheng died, he was summoned to restore his office and promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng's death he was recalled to office and promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 政府惡李植、江東之及思孝輩。

translations.literal: The government disliked Li Zhi, Jiang Dongzhi, and Sixiao's group.
translations.idiomatic: The ruling faction despised Li Zhi, Jiang Dongzhi, and men of Sixiao's circle.

sentences.zh: 思孝遷太常少卿，御史龔仲慶希指詆之，思孝遂求去，不許。

translations.literal: Sixiao was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Rites; Censor Gong Zhongqing attacked him to suit others' wishes; Sixiao then asked to leave, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiao was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Rites; Censor Gong Zhongqing attacked him to curry favor; Sixiao then asked to resign, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 尋遷順天府尹，坐寬縱冒籍舉人，貶三秩視事。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Prefect of Shuntian Prefecture; for leniency in allowing impostors in the examination registry he was demoted three ranks yet continued in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Prefect of Shuntian; for laxity in permitting false registrants among examination candidates he was demoted three ranks but kept at his post.

sentences.zh: 思孝禦三品服自若，被劾，調南京太仆卿，仍貶三秩。

translations.literal: Sixiao wore third-rank robes as before; after being impeached he was transferred to Minister of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing, and again demoted three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiao continued to wear third-rank robes as though nothing had changed; impeached, he was transferred to Minister of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing and demoted three ranks again.

sentences.zh: 未幾，謝病歸。

translations.literal: Before long he resigned on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書陸光祖起為南京光祿卿。

translations.literal: Lu Guangzu, Minister of Personnel, raised him to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Guangzu, Minister of Personnel, recalled him as Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 尋進右僉都御史，巡撫挾西。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and toured Shaanxi as grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right and appointed Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 寧夏哱拜叛，詔思孝移駐下馬關，為總督魏學曾聲援。

translations.literal: When Pida rebelled in Ningxia, the emperor ordered Sixiao to shift his headquarters to Xiamaguan to lend support to the supreme commander Wei Xueceng.
translations.idiomatic: When Pida rebelled in Ningxia, the court ordered Sixiao to move his headquarters to Xiamaguan to reinforce the supreme commander Wei Xueceng.

sentences.zh: 思孝以兵少，請募浙江及宣、大騎卒各五千，發內帑供軍，並乞宥故都御史李材罪，令立功。

translations.literal: Sixiao, because troops were few, asked to recruit five thousand mounted soldiers each from Zhejiang and from Xuanfu and Datong, to disburse from the inner treasury for the army, and also begged pardon for the former Censor-in-Chief Li Cai's crime, enabling him to earn merit through service.
translations.idiomatic: Finding his forces inadequate, Sixiao asked to raise five thousand cavalry each from Zhejiang and from Xuanfu and Datong, to fund the army from the privy purse, and to pardon the former Censor-in-Chief Li Cai so that he might redeem himself in battle.

sentences.zh: 詔思孝近地召募，而罷材勿遣。

translations.literal: The imperial order had Sixiao recruit nearby, and dismissed Li Cai without sending him.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Sixiao to recruit locally and refused to send Li Cai.

sentences.zh: 思孝與學曾議軍事不合，給事中侯慶遠劾思孝舍門戶而守堂奧，設邏卒以衛妻孥，不任封疆事。

translations.literal: Sixiao and Xueceng disagreed on military affairs; Supervising Secretary Hou Qingyuan impeached Sixiao for abandoning the outer gates to guard the inner hall, posting patrol guards to protect wife and children, and being unfit for frontier duty.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiao and Xueceng clashed over military strategy; Supervising Secretary Hou Qingyuan impeached Sixiao for abandoning the frontier to shelter in the inner quarters, posting patrols to guard his wife and children, and being unfit for border command.

sentences.zh: 改撫河南，辭不赴。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to tour Henan but declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned to Henan as grand coordinator, he declined and did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 頃之，召為大理卿。

translations.literal: Shortly after he was summoned as President of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned as President of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 中官郝金詐傳懿旨下獄，刑部薄其罪，思孝駁誅之。

translations.literal: Eunuch Hao Jin forged and transmitted an order from the Empress Dowager and was imprisoned; the Ministry of Punishments treated his crime lightly; Sixiao rejected this and had him sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Hao Jin was imprisoned for forging an order in the Empress Dowager's name; the Ministry of Punishments treated the offense leniently, but Sixiao overturned the ruling and had him sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，進工部左侍郎。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to Left Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to Left Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 陜西織羊絨為民患，以思孝奏，減十之四。

translations.literal: Shaanxi's weaving of camel-hair fleece was a plague on the people; on Sixiao's memorial it was reduced by four tenths.
translations.idiomatic: The weaving of camel-hair fleece in Shaanxi had become a scourge on the people; on Sixiao's memorial the levy was cut by two fifths.

sentences.zh: 進右都御史，協理戎政。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Censor-in-Chief of the Right and assisted in administering military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Right and given charge of military administration.

sentences.zh: 初，廷推李禎為首，思孝次之，帝特用思孝。

translations.literal: At first the court recommended Li Zhen first and Sixiao second; the emperor specially appointed Sixiao.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the court had recommended Li Zhen first and Sixiao second, but the emperor chose Sixiao over the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 或疑有奧援，給事中楊東明、鄒廷彥相繼疏劾。

translations.literal: Some suspected he had hidden patronage; Supervising Secretaries Yang Dongming and Zou Tingyan impeached him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Some suspected he enjoyed secret backing; Supervising Secretaries Yang Dongming and Zou Tingyan impeached him in turn.

sentences.zh: 帝以廷彥受東明指，謫東明，奪廷彥俸。

translations.literal: The emperor held that Tingyan had followed Dongming's lead, demoted Dongming, and stripped Tingyan of salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that Tingyan had acted at Dongming's instigation, demoted Dongming, and stripped Tingyan of his salary.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，吏部尚書孫丕揚掌外察，黜參政丁此呂。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Sun Piyang as Minister of Personnel supervised the outer assessment and dismissed Vice Commissioner Ding Cilü.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Sun Piyang, as Minister of Personnel, oversaw the outer evaluation and dismissed Vice Commissioner Ding Cilü.

sentences.zh: 思孝與東之素善此呂。

translations.literal: Sixiao and Dongzhi had long been on good terms with Cilü.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiao and Dongzhi had long been friendly with Cilü.

sentences.zh: 會御史趙文炳劾文選郎蔣時馨受賄，時馨疑思孝嗾之，遂訐思孝先庇此呂，後求吏部不得，以此二事憾已，遂結江東之、劉應秋等，令李三才屬文炳。

translations.literal: It happened that Censor Zhao Wenbing impeached Jiang Shixin, Director of the Bureau of Appointments, for taking bribes; Shixin suspected Sixiao had instigated it, and thereupon denounced Sixiao for first shielding Cilü and later failing to obtain an appointment from the Ministry of Personnel—bearing resentment over these two matters—and thus joined Jiang Dongzhi, Liu Yingqiu, and others, having Li San'cai direct Wenbing.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Zhao Wenbing impeached Jiang Shixin of the Appointments Bureau for bribery, Shixin suspected Sixiao had put him up to it and accused Sixiao of first shielding Cilü and later failing to win him a post at the Ministry of Personnel; nursing these grievances, he allied with Jiang Dongzhi, Liu Yingqiu, and others and had Li San'cai set Wenbing in motion.

sentences.zh: 帝惡時馨，罷其官。

translations.literal: The emperor detested Shixin and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor despised Shixin and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 思孝等疏辨，且求去。

translations.literal: Sixiao and others submitted memorials in defense and also asked to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiao and his allies submitted memorials in their defense and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 丕揚言時馨無罪，此呂受贓有狀，思孝不當庇。

translations.literal: Piyang said Shixin was innocent, that Cilü had clearly taken bribes, and that Sixiao ought not to have shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: Piyang declared Shixin innocent, held that Cilü's guilt of bribery was established, and argued that Sixiao should not have protected him.

sentences.zh: 因上此呂訪單，乞歸。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted Cilü's investigation slip and asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted Cilü's investigation slip and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 訪單者，吏部當察時，咨公論以定賢否，廷臣因得書所聞以投掌察者。

translations.literal: An investigation slip: when the Ministry of Personnel conducts an assessment, it consults public opinion to determine worth; court ministers may therefore write what they have heard and submit it to the one in charge of the assessment.
translations.idiomatic: An investigation slip was a document through which, at evaluation time, the Ministry of Personnel consulted public opinion to judge merit; court officials could record what they had heard and submit it to the officer conducting the review.

sentences.zh: 事率核實，然間有因以中所惡者。

translations.literal: Matters are generally verified, yet occasionally someone is struck through whom the writer hates.
translations.idiomatic: Reports were usually checked against fact, yet now and then a personal enemy was struck down through the process.

sentences.zh: 帝降詔慰留丕揚，逮此呂，詰讓思孝。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict to comfort and retain Piyang, arrest Cilü, and rebuke Sixiao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict reassuring Piyang and urging him to stay, ordered Cilü arrested, and rebuked Sixiao.

sentences.zh: 御史俞價、強思、馮從吾，給事中黃運泰、祝世祿，皆為時馨訟冤，語侵思孝、東之。

translations.literal: Censors Yu Jia, Qiang Si, Feng Congwu, and Supervising Secretaries Huang Yuntai and Zhu Shilu all pleaded Shixin's innocence, their words impinging on Sixiao and Dongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Yu Jia, Qiang Si, and Feng Congwu, and Supervising Secretaries Huang Yuntai and Zhu Shilu, all pleaded Shixin's innocence, their language turning against Sixiao and Dongzhi.

sentences.zh: 給事中楊天民、馬經綸、馬文卿又各疏劾思孝，大抵言文炳之疏由思孝，藉以搖丕揚也。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Yang Tianmin, Ma Jinglun, and Ma Wenqing again each memorialized to impeach Sixiao, broadly saying Wenbing's memorial came from Sixiao, by which means to shake Piyang.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Yang Tianmin, Ma Jinglun, and Ma Wenqing each memorialized to impeach Sixiao, arguing broadly that Wenbing's memorial originated with Sixiao as a means to undermine Piyang.

sentences.zh: 思孝屢乞罷，因詆丕揚負國。

translations.literal: Sixiao repeatedly begged to be dismissed and thereby slandered Piyang as failing the state.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiao repeatedly asked to be dismissed and denounced Piyang as betraying the state.

sentences.zh: 員外郎嶽元聲言大臣相攻，宜兩罷，似並論丕揚、思孝，而其指特攻時馨以及丕揚。

translations.literal: Vice Director Yue Yuansheng said the great ministers were attacking one another and both ought to be dismissed—seeming to discuss both Piyang and Sixiao, yet his aim was especially to attack Shixin and Piyang.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yue Yuansheng argued that the senior ministers were tearing one another apart and both sides ought to go—appearing to address Piyang and Sixiao alike, yet aiming chiefly at Shixin and Piyang.

sentences.zh: 疏方上，文炳忽變其說，謂：「元聲、東之述思孝意，迫之救此呂、劾時馨，非己意也。

translations.literal: The memorial had just been submitted when Wenbing suddenly changed his story, saying: "Yuansheng and Dongzhi stated Sixiao's intent, forced me to save Cilü and impeach Shixin—it was not my own intent.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the memorial been submitted when Wenbing abruptly reversed himself, claiming: "Yuansheng and Dongzhi relayed Sixiao's wishes and pressured me to save Cilü and impeach Shixin—it was not my own doing.

sentences.zh: 帝皆置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor set all aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let all of it pass without investigation.

sentences.zh: 思孝素以直節高天下，然尚氣好勝，動輒多忤，以此呂故，頗被物議。

translations.literal: Sixiao had long been esteemed throughout the realm for upright integrity, yet he cherished his pride and loved victory, frequently giving offense on many sides; because of Cilü he drew considerable public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiao had long been renowned for upright integrity, yet he was proud and combative, quick to give offense; the Cilü affair brought him considerable public censure.

sentences.zh: 然時馨、此呂皆非端人，丕揚、思孝亦各有所左右。

translations.literal: Yet neither Shixin nor Cilü were upright men; Piyang and Sixiao also each had those they favored.
translations.idiomatic: Yet neither Shixin nor Cilü was an upright man, and both Piyang and Sixiao had their own favorites.

sentences.zh: 其明年，御史林培請辨忠邪，又力詆思孝、東之；

translations.literal: The next year Censor Lin Pei asked to distinguish loyalty from treachery and again fiercely denounced Sixiao and Dongzhi;
translations.idiomatic: The following year Censor Lin Pei petitioned to distinguish loyal from treacherous ministers and again fiercely attacked Sixiao and Dongzhi;

sentences.zh: 且言：「丕揚杜門半載，辭疏十上，意必得請而後已。

translations.literal: and said: "Piyang has shut his doors for half a year, resignation memorials submitted ten times—his intent is surely not to stop until his request is granted.
translations.idiomatic: adding: "Piyang has kept his doors shut for half a year and submitted ten resignation memorials—he plainly will not rest until his request is granted.

sentences.zh: 思孝則杜門未幾，近見從吾、運泰等罷，謂朝廷不難去言官五六人以安我。

translations.literal: Sixiao has shut his doors only a short while; seeing Congwu, Yuntai, and others dismissed lately, he thinks the court would not find it hard to remove five or six remonstrating officials to appease him.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiao has barely shut his doors; seeing Congwu, Yuntai, and others dismissed of late, he assumes the court would not hesitate to remove five or six remonstrating officials to placate him.

sentences.zh: 此人不去，為朝端害。」

translations.literal: If this man is not removed, he will be a harm at the head of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Unless this man is removed, he will poison the summit of the court.

sentences.zh: 帝顧思孝厚，謫培官。

translations.literal: The emperor, regarding Sixiao with favor, demoted Pei in office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, who favored Sixiao, demoted Pei.

sentences.zh: 乾清宮災，思孝請行皇長子冠禮以回天心。

translations.literal: When the Palace of Heavenly Purity caught fire, Sixiao asked that the crown prince's capping ceremony be performed to turn back Heaven's mind.
translations.idiomatic: When the Palace of Heavenly Purity burned, Sixiao urged that the heir apparent's capping ceremony be held to win back Heaven's favor.

sentences.zh: 又以日本封事大壞，請亟修戰守備，並論趙誌臯、石星誤國。

translations.literal: He also said the Japanese enfeoffment affair had gone badly ruinous, asked urgently to repair war preparations and defenses, and together impeached Zhao Zhigao and Shi Xing for misleading the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the Japanese investiture negotiations had collapsed disastrously, urged immediate strengthening of defenses, and impeached Zhao Zhigao and Shi Xing for misleading the state.

sentences.zh: 其秋，丕揚去位，思孝亦引疾，詔馳傳歸，朝端議論始息。

translations.literal: That autumn Piyang left office; Sixiao also cited illness; he was ordered to return home by fast courier; courthead debate finally quieted.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Piyang left office; Sixiao too pleaded illness and was ordered home by express relay; the wrangling at court finally subsided.

sentences.zh: 久之，丕揚復起為吏部，御史史記事復詆思孝與顧天飐合謀欲構陷丕揚。

translations.literal: After a long while Piyang was again raised as Minister of Personnel; Censor Shi Jishi again slandered Sixiao and Gu Tian-song as plotting together to frame Piyang.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Piyang was recalled as Minister of Personnel; Censor Shi Jishi again accused Sixiao and Gu Tiansong of conspiring to entrap him.

sentences.zh: 顧憲成、高攀龍力辨其誣，而思孝卒矣。

translations.literal: Gu Xiancheng and Gao Panlong strenuously argued the slander was false, but Sixiao had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xiancheng and Gao Panlong vigorously refuted the accusation, but by then Sixiao was already dead.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 丁此呂，字右武，新建人。

translations.literal: Ding Cilü, styled Youwu, a native of Xinjian.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Cilü, courtesy name Youwu, was a native of Xinjian.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fifth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 由漳州推官征授御史。

translations.literal: From investigating censor of Zhangzhou he was summoned and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned from his post as judicial assistant at Zhangzhou, he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 慈寧宮災，請撤鰲山，停織造、燒造，還建言譴謫諸臣，去張居正余黨，速誅徐爵、遊七。

translations.literal: When the Cining Palace caught fire, he asked to remove the Ao Mountain displays, halt imperial weaving and kiln works, restore censured remonstrating ministers, remove Zhang Juzheng's remaining faction, and swiftly execute Xu Jue and You Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Cining Palace burned, he urged removal of the lantern displays, a halt to imperial weaving and kiln production, restoration of censured remonstrators, purge of Zhang Juzheng's remaining followers, and swift execution of Xu Jue and You Qi.

sentences.zh: 報聞。

translations.literal: The reply noted his request.
translations.idiomatic: The court acknowledged his memorial.

sentences.zh: 尋劾禮部侍郎高啟愚命題示禪授意，謫潞安推官。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached Vice Minister of Rites Gao Qiyu for examination questions hinting at abdication and succession, and was demoted to investigating censor of Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached Vice Minister of Rites Gao Qiyu for examination questions hinting at abdication and succession, and was himself demoted to judicial assistant at Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 語詳《李植傳》。

translations.literal: The account is given in detail in the biography of Li Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in the biography of Li Zhi.

sentences.zh: 尋遷太仆丞，歷浙江右參政。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Assistant Minister of the Imperial Stud, and served successively as Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang Right.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Assistant Minister of the Imperial Stud and later served as Right Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 考察論黜，復遣官逮之。

translations.literal: At the assessment he was judged for dismissal, and officials were again sent to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: At the triennial evaluation he was marked for dismissal, and officers were again dispatched to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 大學士趙誌臯等再疏乞宥，且言此呂有氣節，未必果貪汙。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao and others again memorialized begging pardon, and said Cilü had integrity and was not necessarily truly corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao and others again petitioned for clemency, arguing that Cilü was a man of principle and not necessarily guilty of corruption.

sentences.zh: 丕揚亦言此呂無逮問條，乞免送詔獄。

translations.literal: Piyang also said Cilü had no grounds for arrest and interrogation, and begged to exempt him from delivery to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Piyang too argued that Cilü did not meet the criteria for arrest and interrogation, and asked that he not be sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不從，逮下鎮撫，謫戍邊。

translations.literal: The emperor would not consent to any; he was arrested and sent down to the Brocade Guard, then banished to frontier garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused all appeals; Cilü was arrested, handed to the Brocade Guard, and exiled to frontier garrison duty.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：劉臺諸人，皆以論張居正得罪。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: Liu Tai and the others all offended because they remonstrated against Zhang Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Liu Tai and his fellows all fell afoul of power because they criticized Zhang Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 罰最重者，名亦最高。

translations.literal: Those punished most severely also bear the highest renown.
translations.idiomatic: Those who suffered the harshest penalties won the highest renown.

sentences.zh: 用汲之免也，幸耳。

translations.literal: That Yongji was spared was mere fortune.
translations.idiomatic: That Yongji escaped punishment was mere luck.

sentences.zh: 平心論之，居正為相，於國事不為無功；

translations.literal: Speaking impartially, Juzheng as chief minister did not render the state without merit;
translations.idiomatic: Judged fairly, Juzheng as chief minister did not serve the state without merit;

sentences.zh: 諸人論之，不無過當。

translations.literal: The others' criticisms of him were not without excess.
translations.idiomatic: yet their attacks on him were not without excess.

sentences.zh: 然聞謗而不知懼，忿戾怨毒，務快己意。

translations.literal: Yet when he heard slander he did not know fear; he was resentful, cruel, and spiteful, bent on gratifying his own will.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he heard criticism he felt no fear; resentful, cruel, and spiteful, he was bent on having his own way.

sentences.zh: 虧盈好還，禍釀身後。

translations.literal: When fullness is exhausted return is favored; disaster brewed after his death.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's balance demands repayment; the disaster he brewed came after his death.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「惟善人能受盡言。」

translations.literal: The tradition says, "Only the good man can receive the fullest remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says, "Only the good man can bear the fullest remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 於戲難哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how difficult!
